title.raw: 卷30 王建 安同 樓伏連 丘堆 娥清 劉尼 奚眷 車伊洛等 Volume 30: Wang Jian, An Tong, Lou Fulian, Qiu Dui, E Qing, Liu Ni, Xi Juan, Cheyi Luodeng

sentences.zh: 王建 安同 樓伏連 丘堆 娥清 劉尼 奚眷 車伊洛 宿石 來大千 周幾 豆代田 周觀 閭大肥 尉撥 陸真 呂洛拔

translations.literal: Wang Jian; An Tong; Lou Fulian; Qiu Dui; E Qing; Liu Ni; Xi Juan; Che Yiluo; Su Shi; Lai Daqian; Zhou Ji; Dou Daitian; Zhou Guan; Lü Dafei; Wei Bo; Lu Zhen; Lü Luoba
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian; An Tong; Lou Fulian; Qiu Dui; E Qing; Liu Ni; Xi Juan; Che Yiluo; Su Shi; Lai Daqian; Zhou Ji; Dou Daitian; Zhou Guan; Lü Dafei; Wei Bo; Lu Zhen; Lü Luoba

sentences.zh: 王建，廣寧人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was a man of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian came from Guangning.

sentences.zh: 祖姑為平文后，生昭成皇帝。

translations.literal: His paternal aunt was Empress Pingwen and bore Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father's aunt had been Empress Pingwen and bore Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 伯祖豐，以帝舅貴重。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Feng was honored as the emperor's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Feng had risen high as the emperor's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 豐子支，尚昭成女，甚見親待。

translations.literal: Feng's son Zhi married a daughter of Zhaocheng and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's son Zhi married a daughter of Emperor Zhaocheng and enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 建少尚公主。

translations.literal: Jian in his youth married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: While still young, Jian married a princess.

sentences.zh: 登國初，為外朝大人，與和跋等十三人迭典庶事，參與計謀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he became an outer-court dignitary; with He Ba and twelve others he took turns overseeing routine affairs and took part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Dengguo era he was made an outer-court dignitary. He and He Ba and twelve others rotated in charge of routine business and joined in counsel.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸濡源，遣建使慕容垂，辭色高亢，垂壯之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor visited Ruyuan he sent Jian as envoy to Murong Chui; his words and bearing were lofty, and Chui admired him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu visited Ruyuan he sent Jian to Murong Chui. Jian's tone and bearing were commanding, and Chui was impressed.

sentences.zh: 還為左大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Left Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Left Grandee.

sentences.zh: [1]建兄回，諸子多不順法，建具以狀聞，回父子伏誅。

translations.literal: [1] Jian's elder brother Hui—his sons for the most part did not obey the law. Jian reported the full facts, and Hui and his sons were executed.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Jian's elder brother Hui had sons who for the most part flouted the law. Jian laid out the facts in full, and Hui and his sons were put to death.

sentences.zh: 其謹直如此。

translations.literal: His scrupulous uprightness was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his scrupulous integrity.

sentences.zh: 從征伐諸國，破二十餘部，以功賜奴婢數十口，雜畜數千，從征衞辰，破之，賜僮隸五千戶，[2]為中部大人。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against the various states and broke more than twenty divisions; for merit he was given several tens of male and female servants and several thousand mixed livestock. In the campaign against Wei Chen he broke them and was given five thousand households of bondsmen; [2] he became Central-Region Chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in campaigns against the various states and shattered more than twenty tribal divisions. For his merit he received several dozen bondsmen and bondswomen and several thousand head of mixed livestock. On the campaign against Wei Chen he defeated them and was granted five thousand households of bondsmen. [2] He was made chieftain of the central region.

sentences.zh: 從破慕容寶於參合陂。

translations.literal: He followed in the defeat of Murong Bao at Canhe Slope.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the defeat of Murong Bao at Canhe Slope.

sentences.zh: 太祖乘勝將席卷南夏，於是簡擇俘眾，有才能者留之，其餘欲悉給衣糧遣歸，令中州之民咸知恩德。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor, riding his victory, was about to sweep through the southern Xia. He therefore selected among the captives those with ability to keep, while the rest he wished to supply fully with clothing and grain and send home, so that the people of the central provinces might all know his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu, pressing his victory, meant to sweep through the southern Xia. He sorted the captives, keeping those with talent and intending to clothe and feed the rest and send them home so that the people of the central provinces would know his grace.

sentences.zh: 乃召羣臣議之。

translations.literal: He then summoned the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: He then called the ministers together to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 建曰：「慕容寶覆敗於此，國內虛空，圖之為易。

translations.literal: Jian said: "Murong Bao has been utterly defeated here; within the state all is empty—it would be easy to scheme against them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Murong Bao has been crushed here. His realm stands hollow within—it would be easy to strike."

sentences.zh: 今獲而歸之，無乃不可乎？

translations.literal: Now to capture them and send them back—would that not be inadmissible?
translations.idiomatic: To seize them now only to release them—would that not be folly?

sentences.zh: 且縱敵生患，不如殺之。

translations.literal: Moreover, to spare the enemy breeds trouble; better to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, sparing the enemy breeds future harm. Better to kill them.

sentences.zh: 」太祖謂諸將曰：「若從建言，吾恐後南人創乂，絕其向化之心，非伐罪弔民之義。

translations.literal: " The Taizu Emperor said to the generals: "If I follow Jian's counsel, I fear that later the southern people will be newly wounded and their hearts turned from submission—this is not the meaning of punishing crime and comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizu told the generals, "If I follow Jian's advice, I fear the southerners will be freshly wounded and turn from us—far from the purpose of punishing wrong and comforting the people."

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸以建言為然，建又固執，乃坑之。

translations.literal: " The generals all agreed that Jian's counsel was right; Jian again held firm, and they were buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals all sided with Jian. Jian held his ground, and the captives were buried alive.

sentences.zh: 太祖既而悔焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor afterward regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu later came to regret it.

sentences.zh: 後從征慕容寶，拜冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign against Murong Bao and was appointed General Who Crowns the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the campaign against Murong Bao and was made General Who Crowns the Army.

sentences.zh: 并州既平，車駕東出井陘，命建率五萬騎先驅啟路。

translations.literal: When Bingzhou was pacified the imperial carriage went east through Jingxing Pass; Jian was ordered to lead fifty thousand horsemen as vanguard to open the road.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bingzhou was pacified, the imperial carriage marched east through Jingxing Pass. Jian was ordered to lead fifty thousand horsemen ahead to clear the way.

sentences.zh: 車駕次常山，諸郡皆降，惟中山、鄴、信都三城不下。

translations.literal: The carriage halted at Changshan; all the commanderies submitted save Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu—three cities that would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The court halted at Changshan. Every commandery surrendered except Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu, which held out.

sentences.zh: 乃遣衞王儀南攻鄴，建攻信都，眾各五萬。

translations.literal: He then sent Prince Wei of Wei south to attack Ye and Jian to attack Xindu, each with fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Wei of Wei south against Ye and Jian against Xindu, fifty thousand men apiece.

sentences.zh: 建等攻城六十餘日不能克，士卒多傷。

translations.literal: Jian and the others besieged the cities for more than sixty days without taking them; the soldiers suffered many wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and his fellows besieged their cities for more than sixty days without success, and the troops took heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃自中山幸信都，慕容寶冀州刺史慕容鳳夜踰城走，信都降。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor then came in person from Zhongshan to Xindu; Murong Bao's Inspector of Jizhou Murong Feng fled the city by night over the walls, and Xindu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu came in person from Zhongshan to Xindu. Murong Feng, Murong Bao's inspector of Jizhou, fled over the wall by night, and Xindu submitted.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸鉅鹿，破慕容寶於栢肆塢，遂進圍中山。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Julu, defeated Murong Bao at Baixi Wu, and advanced to besiege Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The court reached Julu, defeated Murong Bao at Baixi Wu, and pressed on to besiege Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 寶棄城走和龍，城內無主，百姓惶惑，東門不閉。

translations.literal: Bao abandoned the city and fled to Helong; within the walls there was no master, the people were alarmed, and the east gate stood unclosed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao abandoned the city and fled to Helong. With no ruler within, the people were in turmoil, and the east gate lay open.

sentences.zh: 太祖將夜入乘城，據守其門。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor was about to enter the city by night, scale the walls, and hold the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu meant to enter by night, scale the wall, and seize the gates.

sentences.zh: 建貪而無謀，意在虜獲，恐士卒肆掠，盜亂府庫，請俟天明，太祖乃止。

translations.literal: Jian, greedy and without plan, had his mind on booty; fearing the soldiers would plunder at will and pillage the treasuries, he asked to wait until daybreak, and the Taizu Emperor desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was greedy and shortsighted, bent on loot. He feared the troops would run wild and ransack the storehouses, and asked to wait for dawn. Emperor Taizu held back.

sentences.zh: 是夜，徒河人共立慕容普驎為主，遂閉門固守。

translations.literal: That night the people of Tuhe together installed Murong Pulü as lord, closed the gates, and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: That night the people of Tuhe together raised Murong Pulü as their leader, shut the gates, and dug in.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃悉眾攻之，連日不拔。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor then threw his full strength against it; for days he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu then threw his full force against the city, but for days could not break it.

sentences.zh: 使人登巢車臨城，招其眾曰：「慕容寶捐城奔走，汝曹百姓將為誰守？

translations.literal: He had a man mount a siege tower overlooking the wall and call to the multitude: "Murong Bao cast away the city and fled—whom do you common people mean to hold it for?
translations.idiomatic: He sent a man up a siege tower to overlook the wall and call out, "Murong Bao threw away the city and fled. For whom do you people mean to hold it?"

sentences.zh: 何不識天命，取死亡也？

translations.literal: Why not recognize Heaven's mandate and avoid death?
translations.idiomatic: Why not bow to Heaven's mandate and spare yourselves a pointless death?

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「羣小無知，但復恐如參合之眾，故求全月日之命耳。

translations.literal: " They all said: "We petty folk are ignorant; we only fear again becoming like the multitude at Canhe—so we ask merely to keep our lives for a month or a day.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "We are ignorant folk. We only fear sharing the fate of the captives at Canhe—we want no more than to live out another month or day."

sentences.zh: 」太祖聞之，顧視建而唾其面。

translations.literal: " When the Taizu Emperor heard this he turned, looked at Jian, and spat in his face.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Taizu heard this he turned, looked at Jian, and spat in his face.

sentences.zh: 中山平，賜建爵濮陽公。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified Jian was enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell, Jian was enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 烏丸庫傉官鳴聚黨為寇，[3]詔建討平之。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan Kuluguan Ming gathered a faction and raided as bandits; [3] an edict ordered Jian to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan Kuluguan Ming gathered followers and raided as bandits. [3] An edict sent Jian to crush them.

sentences.zh: 遷太僕，徙為真定公，加散騎常侍、冀青二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Stud, moved to Duke of Zhending, and given the additional posts of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Inspector of Ji and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of the Stud, transferred to Duke of Zhending, and given the additional titles of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and inspector of Ji and Qing.

sentences.zh: 卒，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 初，建兄豆居以建功賜爵即丘侯，無子，建以子斤襲兄爵。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jian's elder brother Douju had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiqiu for achievements; having no son, Jian had his son Jin succeed to his brother's title.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jian's elder brother Douju had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiqiu for merit but left no son. Jian had his son Jin inherit the brother's title.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，給事中，任職用事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's reign he was Attendant-in-Ordinary and wielded power in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Taizong's reign he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and held real power.

sentences.zh: 轉大長秋。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Director of the Palace Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Director of the Palace Retinue.

sentences.zh: 世祖征赫連昌，遣斤部造攻具。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang he sent Jin to supply siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang he sent Jin to furnish siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 進爵淮南公，加平北將軍。

translations.literal: Jin was advanced to Duke of Huainan and given the additional post of General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was promoted to Duke of Huainan and made General Who Pacifies the North as well.

sentences.zh: 時并州胡酋田卜謀反誅，餘眾不安，遣斤鎮慮虒以撫慰之。

translations.literal: At the time the Hu chieftain Tian Bu of Bingzhou had been executed for plotting rebellion; the remaining followers were unsettled, and Jin was sent to garrison Lüsi to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu chieftain Tian Bu of Bingzhou had just been executed for rebellion, and his followers were uneasy. Jin was sent to garrison Lüsi to calm them.

sentences.zh: [4]斤綏靜胡魏，甚收聲稱。

translations.literal: [4] Jin pacified the Hu and Wei and won a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Jin quieted the Hu and Wei tribes and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆遣將到彥之寇河南，世祖西征赫連定，以斤為衞兵將軍，鎮蒲坂。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong sent the general Dao Yanzhi to invade Henan; Emperor Shizu marched west against Helian Ding and made Jin General of the Palace Guards, garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent the general Dao Yanzhi against Henan. Emperor Shizu marched west against Helian Ding and made Jin General of the Palace Guards, stationed at Puban.

sentences.zh: 關隴平，斤徙鎮長安，假節、鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: When Guan and Long were pacified Jin was moved to garrison Chang'an with brevet staff and the title General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan and Long were pacified, Jin was shifted to garrison Chang'an with brevet staff as General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 斤遂驕矜，不順法度，信用左右，調役百姓，民不堪之，南奔漢川者數千家。

translations.literal: Jin then grew arrogant, did not obey the laws, trusted his favorites, and levied corvée on the people until they could not bear it; several thousand households fled south to Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then grew arrogant and lawless, trusted his intimates, and pressed the people with labor until they could not endure it. Several thousand households fled south into Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 而委罪於雍州刺史陽文祖、秦州刺史任延明。

translations.literal: Yet he laid the blame on Yang Wenzu, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Ren Yanming, Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then shifted the blame onto Yang Wenzu, inspector of Yongzhou, and Ren Yanming, inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖召問二人，各以狀對。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu summoned and questioned the two men; each answered according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu summoned the two men and questioned them. Each answered on the facts.

sentences.zh: 世祖知為斤所誣，遣宜陽公伏樹覆按虛實，得數十事。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Jin had slandered them and sent Duke of Yiyang Fu Shu to investigate; several dozen matters were proved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that Jin had slandered them and sent Duke of Yiyang Fu Shu to investigate. Dozens of charges were confirmed.

sentences.zh: 遂斬斤以徇。

translations.literal: Jin was then beheaded as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was beheaded as a warning to all.

sentences.zh: 子安都，襲，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: His son Andu inherited; the title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Andu inherited the line, but the rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 世祖拜為太子庶子，出為鄯善鎮將。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu appointed him Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and then sent him out as garrison commander of Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu made him Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, then sent him out as garrison commander of Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，為內都大官。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozong he was Grand Director of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he served as Grand Director of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，子買得襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Maide inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his son Maide inherited.

sentences.zh: 建曾孫樹，以善射有寵於顯祖，為內侍長。

translations.literal: Jian's great-grandson Shu, skilled in archery, won favor with Emperor Xianzu and became Chief Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's great-grandson Shu, a fine archer, won favor with Emperor Xianzu and became chief palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書，賜爵歷陽侯，加龍驤將軍、員外常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Minister, enfeoffed as Marquis of Liyang, and given the additional posts of General of the Flying Dragon and Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to Minister, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liyang, and given the additional titles of General of the Flying Dragon and Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 出為平西將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 安同，遼東胡人也。

translations.literal: An Tong was a man of the Hu of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: An Tong was a Hu from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 其先祖曰世高，漢時以安息王侍子入洛。

translations.literal: His remote ancestor was called Shigao; in Han times he entered Luoyang as the hostage son of the king of Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: His remote ancestor was called Shigao, who in Han times had entered Luoyang as the hostage son of the king of Parthia.

sentences.zh: 歷魏至晉，避亂遼東，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Through Wei down to Jin, fleeing turmoil he went to Liaodong and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wei and into Jin, fleeing turmoil, the family settled in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 父屈，仕慕容暐，為殿中郎將。

translations.literal: His father Qu served Murong Wei as Commandant of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qu had served Murong Wei as Commandant of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 苻堅滅暐，屈友人公孫眷之妹沒入苻氏宮，出賜劉庫仁為妻。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian destroyed Wei, the younger sister of Qu's friend Gongsun Juan was taken into the Fu palace and then given out to Liu Kuren as wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian destroyed Murong Wei, the younger sister of Qu's friend Gongsun Juan was seized for the Fu palace, then given to Liu Kuren as wife.

sentences.zh: 庫仁貴寵之。

translations.literal: Kuren honored and favored her.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren prized and favored her.

sentences.zh: 同因隨眷商販，見太祖有濟世之才，遂留奉侍。

translations.literal: Tong followed Juan in trade, saw that the Taizu Emperor had talent to save the age, and stayed to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had followed Juan in trade, saw in Emperor Taizu the talent to redeem the age, and remained to serve him.

sentences.zh: 性端嚴明惠，好長者之言。

translations.literal: His nature was upright, strict, clear, and discerning; he loved the words of elders.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright, strict, and clear-minded, and loved the counsel of his elders.

sentences.zh: 登國初，太祖徵兵於慕容垂，事在窟咄傳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo the Taizu Emperor sought troops from Murong Chui—the matter is in the biography of Kudi.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Dengguo, Emperor Taizu sought troops from Murong Chui—the account is in the biography of Kudi.

sentences.zh: 同頻使稱旨，遂見寵異，以為外朝大人，與和跋等出入禁中，迭典庶事，太祖班賜功臣，同以使功居多，賜以妻妾及隸戶三十，馬二匹，羊五十口，加廣武將軍。

translations.literal: Tong went often as envoy and hit the mark; he was favored exceptionally, made an outer-court dignitary, and with He Ba and others went in and out of the inner palace, taking turns over routine affairs. When the Taizu Emperor distributed rewards to meritorious ministers, Tong's envoy service counted for the most; he was given wives and concubines and thirty dependent households, two horses, fifty sheep, and the additional post of General of Broad Might.
translations.idiomatic: Tong served repeatedly as envoy and always pleased the court. He was singled out for favor, made an outer-court dignitary, and with He Ba and others passed in and out of the inner palace, sharing routine duties. When Emperor Taizu rewarded his ministers, Tong's diplomatic service weighed heaviest. He received wives and concubines, thirty dependent households, two horses, fifty sheep, and the additional rank of General of Broad Might.

sentences.zh: 從征姚平於柴壁，姚興悉眾救平，太祖乃增築重圍以拒興。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Yao Ping at Chaibi; Yao Xing brought his full host to rescue Ping, and the Taizu Emperor therefore built an additional heavy encirclement to block Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Yao Ping at Chaibi. Yao Xing marched with his full force to relieve Ping, and Emperor Taizu raised a second ring of entrenchments to block him.

sentences.zh: 同進計曰：「臣受遣詣絳督租，見汾東有蒙坑，東西三百餘里，徑路不通。

translations.literal: Tong offered a plan: "I was sent to Jiang to oversee the land tax and saw east of the Fen a Meng Ravine more than three hundred li from east to west, with no path through.
translations.idiomatic: Tong proposed: "I had been sent to Jiang to collect the land tax and saw east of the Fen a Meng Ravine, more than three hundred li from east to west, with no road through."

sentences.zh: 姚興來，必從汾西，乘高臨下，直至柴壁。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing comes he is sure to take the west bank of the Fen, descend from the heights, and reach Chaibi directly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing comes he will surely take the west bank of the Fen, descend from the heights, and strike Chaibi head-on.

sentences.zh: 如此，則寇內外勢接，重圍難固，不可制也。

translations.literal: In that case the enemy's inner and outer forces will join; the heavy encirclement will be hard to hold and cannot be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Then his forces inside and out will link up, the siege will be hard to hold, and we will lose control.

sentences.zh: 宜截汾曲為南北浮橋，乘西岸築圍。

translations.literal: We should cut the Fen's bend with north and south pontoon bridges and build an encirclement on the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: We should span the Fen's bend with pontoon bridges north and south and build a wall on the west bank.

sentences.zh: 西圍既固，賊至無所施其智力矣。

translations.literal: Once the western encirclement is firm, when the enemy arrives he will have nowhere to apply his wits.
translations.idiomatic: Once the western ring is secure, the enemy will have no room to use his stratagems.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " They followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 興果視平屠滅而不能救。

translations.literal: Xing indeed watched Ping slaughtered and could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Xing could only watch as Ping was destroyed and could not save him.

sentences.zh: 以謀功，賜爵北新侯，加安遠將軍。

translations.literal: For this stratagem he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Beixin and given the additional post of General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: For this counsel he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Beixin and made General Who Pacifies the Distance as well.

sentences.zh: 詔同送姚興將越騎校尉唐小方等於長安。

translations.literal: An edict had Tong escort Yao Xing's general, Commandant of Swift Cavalry Tang Xiaofang, and others to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Tong to escort Yao Xing's general Tang Xiaofang, Commandant of Swift Cavalry, and others to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 世祖監國，臨朝聽政，以同為左輔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu oversaw the state and held court to hear government, Tong was made his left assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu oversaw the realm and held court, Tong was made his left assistant.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河南，拜同右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned in Henan, Tong was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned in Henan, Tong was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the Right.

sentences.zh: 世祖出鎮北境，同與安定王彌留鎮京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu went out to garrison the northern frontier, Tong and Prince of Anding Mi remained to garrison the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu went north to garrison the frontier, Tong and Prince of Anding Mi stayed to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進爵高陽公，拜光祿勳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne Tong was advanced to Duke of Gaoyang and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Service.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, Tong was raised to Duke of Gaoyang and made Grand Master of Splendid Service.

sentences.zh: 尋除征東大將軍、冀青二州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was removed and made General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Ji and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to General Who Conquers the East and inspector of Ji and Qing.

sentences.zh: 同長子屈，[5]太宗時典太倉事，盜官粳米數石，欲以養親。

translations.literal: Tong's eldest son Qu, [5] in Emperor Taizong's time oversaw the imperial granary affairs and stole several piculs of official rice, intending to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's eldest son Qu, [5] under Emperor Taizong had charge of the imperial granary and stole several piculs of government rice to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 同大怒，奏求戮屈，自劾不能訓子，請罪。

translations.literal: Tong was greatly angered, memorialized asking that Qu be executed, impeached himself for failing to instruct his son, and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was furious. He memorialized asking that Qu be put to death, impeached himself for failing to teach his son, and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉而恕之，遂詔長給同粳米。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong praised this and pardoned him, then ordered that Tong be supplied with rice in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong praised him and pardoned Qu, then ordered that Tong receive a perpetual rice allowance.

sentences.zh: 其公清奉法，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His public integrity and observance of law were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and regard for law were all of this stamp.

sentences.zh: 同在官明察，長於校練，家法修整，為世所稱。

translations.literal: While in office Tong was clear-sighted, skilled in drill and inspection, and kept his household rules in order—praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: In office Tong was keen-sighted and skilled at drill and review. His household discipline was strict, and the age praised him.

sentences.zh: 及在冀州，年老，頗殖財貨，大興寺塔，為百姓所苦。

translations.literal: When he was in Jizhou, in his old age he amassed wealth, built temples and pagodas on a grand scale, and became a burden to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Jizhou, in his later years, he piled up wealth and raised temples and pagodas on a great scale, to the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengui he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Shengui.

sentences.zh: 追贈高陽王，諡曰恭惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang with the posthumous title Gonghui, "Respectful and Kind."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang with the posthumous name Gonghui, "Respectful and Kind."

sentences.zh: 屈子陽烈，散騎侍郎，賜爵北新子。

translations.literal: Qu's son Yanglie was Gentleman Attendant at Large and enfeoffed as Viscount of Beixin.
translations.idiomatic: Qu's son Yanglie was Gentleman Attendant at Large and enfeoffed as Viscount of Beixin.

sentences.zh: 屈弟原，雅性矜嚴，沉勇多智略。

translations.literal: Qu's younger brother Yuan was by nature reserved and stern, deep and brave, with many stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Qu's younger brother Yuan was by nature reserved and stern, deep-spirited and brave, and rich in stratagems.

sentences.zh: 太宗時為獵郎，出監雲中軍事。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's time he was a Hunting Gentleman and went out to oversee military affairs in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he was a Hunting Gentleman and was sent out to oversee military affairs in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 時赫連屈丐犯河西，原以數十騎擊之，殺十餘人。

translations.literal: At the time Helian Qubugai invaded Hexi; Yuan with several tens of horsemen attacked him and killed more than ten men.
translations.idiomatic: When Helian Qubugai invaded Hexi, Yuan struck him with several dozen horsemen and killed more than ten of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 太宗以原輕敵，違節度，加其罪責。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, because Yuan had taken the enemy lightly and violated military regulations, added blame to his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong held Yuan accountable for underestimating the enemy and disobeying command.

sentences.zh: 然知原驍勇，遂任以為將，鎮守雲中。

translations.literal: Yet knowing Yuan was fierce and brave, he then entrusted him as a general to garrison Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet knowing how fierce and capable Yuan was, he still put him in command and posted him to garrison Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 寬和愛下，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: He was lenient and harmonious, loved those below him, and greatly won the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous and easy with his men, and won their hearts completely.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕屢犯塞，原輒摧破之。

translations.literal: The Rouran repeatedly invaded the frontier; Yuan always crushed and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier again and again, Yuan drove them back every time.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵武原侯，加魯兵將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title Marquis of Wuyuan and additionally named General of Lu Troops.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyuan and made General of Lu Troops.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，徵拜駕部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Imperial Chariot Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu came to the throne, Yuan was summoned to court and appointed Minister of the Imperial Chariot Office.

sentences.zh: 車駕征蠕蠕大檀，分軍五道並進，大檀驚駭北遁。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage campaigned against Datan of the Rouran; the army was divided into five routes advancing together, and Datan, startled and terrified, fled north.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Datan of the Rouran, the army split into five columns and advanced together; Datan, terrified, fled north.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，河間公，加侍中、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Hejian, additionally named Palace Attendant and Great General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Hejian, with the additional titles of Palace Attendant and Great General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 從征赫連昌，入其城而還。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helian Chang, entered their city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Helian Chang, entered the enemy city, and returned.

sentences.zh: 車駕北伐，蠕蠕遁走。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage made a northern campaign; the Rouran fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign the Rouran fled before the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞東部高車在巳尼陂，人畜甚眾，將遣襲之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu heard that the eastern Gaoche were at Sini Lake, with very many people and livestock, and intended to send a raid against them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu learned that the eastern Gaoche were encamped at Sini Lake with vast herds and many people, and planned a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆以為難，世祖不從。

translations.literal: The generals all considered it difficult; Emperor Shizu did not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all thought it too risky, but Emperor Shizu would not be dissuaded.

sentences.zh: 遣原與侍中古弼率萬騎討之，大獲而還。

translations.literal: He sent Yuan and Palace Attendant Gu Bi at the head of ten thousand cavalry to attack them; they gained greatly and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yuan and Palace Attendant Gu Bi with ten thousand cavalry to strike them; they took a great haul and returned.

sentences.zh: 車駕征昌黎，原與建寧王崇屯于漠南以備蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against Changli, Yuan and Prince of Jianning Chong garrisoned south of the desert to guard against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Changli, Yuan and Prince of Jianning Chong were posted south of the desert to guard against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 原在朝無所比周，然恃寵驕恣，多所排抑。

translations.literal: Yuan in court joined no cliques, yet relying on favor he was arrogant and willful, and frequently suppressed others.
translations.idiomatic: In court Yuan kept to no faction, but favored and emboldened he grew arrogant and often pushed others down.

sentences.zh: 為子求襄城公盧魯元女，魯元不許。

translations.literal: He sought the daughter of Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan for his son; Luyuan refused.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan for his daughter's hand for his son; Luyuan refused.

sentences.zh: 原告其罪狀，事相連逮，歷時不決。

translations.literal: Yuan accused him of his crimes; the matter implicated many and dragged on unresolved for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan denounced him on criminal charges; the case dragged on for a long time as more and more people were implicated.

sentences.zh: 原懼不勝，遂謀為逆，事洩伏誅。

translations.literal: Yuan, fearing he would not prevail, then plotted rebellion; the matter leaked out and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would lose, Yuan plotted rebellion; when the plot was exposed he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 臨刑上疏曰：「臣聞聖不獨明而治，鼎不單足而立，是以熒火之光，猶增日月之曜。

translations.literal: Facing execution he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that a sage does not govern by brilliance alone, and a tripod does not stand on a single leg; thus even the light of a glowworm still adds to the radiance of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of execution he submitted a memorial: "I have heard that no sage rules by his light alone, and no tripod stands on one leg; even a glowworm's flame adds something to the brightness of sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 先臣同，往因聖運，歸身太祖，竭誠勠力，立効於險難之中。

translations.literal: My late lord Tong, in former times by the holy fortune, gave himself to Emperor Taizu, exhausted his sincerity and strength, and established merit amid peril and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: My late father Tong, in those days of sacred fortune, pledged himself to Emperor Taizu and gave his full strength, winning merit in the midst of danger.

sentences.zh: 臣以頑闇，忝備股肱。

translations.literal: Your subject, by my dull obtuseness, unworthily serve as the emperor's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: I, dull and unworthy, have been honored to serve as one of Your Majesty's closest ministers.

sentences.zh: 陛下恩育，委以朝政，思展微誠，仰報恩澤。

translations.literal: Your Majesty nurtured me with grace and entrusted me with court governance; I thought to display my slight sincerity and repay your gracious favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty raised me with grace and entrusted me with affairs of state; I meant to show what little loyalty I had and repay that kindness.

sentences.zh: 而魯元姦佞，構成貝錦，天威遂加，合門俱戮。

translations.literal: Yet Luyuan was treacherous and sycophantic, fabricating a tangled web of slander, so imperial wrath fell, and the whole household was executed together.
translations.idiomatic: But Luyuan is treacherous and false; he wove a web of slander, and under heaven's wrath my whole house has been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 此乃命也，非臣之枉。

translations.literal: This is fate—not your subject's wrongful treatment.
translations.idiomatic: This is fate, not injustice done to me alone.

sentences.zh: 但魯元外類忠貞，內懷姦詐，而陛下任以腹心，恐釁發肘腋。

translations.literal: But Luyuan outwardly appears loyal and true, yet inwardly harbors treachery and deceit; Your Majesty entrusts him as a confidant—I fear trouble will break out close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Luyuan wears the face of loyalty while hiding treachery within, and Your Majesty keeps him at your side—I fear disaster will rise from those nearest you.

sentences.zh: 臣與魯元生為怨人，死為讎鬼，非以私故，謗毀魯元。

translations.literal: Your subject and Luyuan were enemies in life and will be vengeful ghosts in death; it is not from personal motive that I slander Luyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Luyuan and I were enemies in life and will be avenging spirits in death; I do not speak against him from private spite.

sentences.zh: 不復眷眷，披露誠款。」

translations.literal: No longer cherishing attachment, I disclose my sincere candor."
translations.idiomatic: I have no further hope of life; I speak only what is true."

sentences.zh: 原弟頡，頡弟聰，為內侍。

translations.literal: Yuan's younger brother Jie, and Jie's younger brother Cong, served as inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's younger brother Jie and Jie's younger brother Cong both served as inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 聰弟蕯，為龍驤將軍、給事黃門侍郎，賜爵廣宗侯。

translations.literal: Cong's younger brother Sa was Dragon Cavalry General and Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, and was granted the title Marquis of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's younger brother Sa became Dragon Cavalry General and Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 原兄弟外節儉，而內實積聚，及誅後，籍其財至數萬。

translations.literal: The Yuan brothers outwardly were frugal, yet inwardly actually amassed wealth; after their execution, their property was confiscated to the amount of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan brothers lived plainly in public while secretly hoarding wealth; after their execution their estates were seized to the value of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 頡，辯慧多策略，最有父風。

translations.literal: Jie was eloquent, clever, and rich in stratagems—most possessed his father's style.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was quick-witted, eloquent, and full of stratagems—the very image of his father.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為內侍長，令察舉百僚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's reign, he was Chief Inner Attendant and ordered to investigate and recommend the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Taizong's reign he was made Chief Inner Attendant and charged with inspecting and reporting on the officials.

sentences.zh: 糾刺姦慝，無所回避。

translations.literal: He exposed and impeached the wicked, sparing none.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed corruption and wrongdoing without fear or favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗告其父陰事，太宗以為忠，特親寵之。

translations.literal: He once reported his father's secret affairs; Emperor Taizong considered this loyalty and especially favored and cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He once denounced his own father's private misconduct; Emperor Taizong took this as proof of loyalty and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 宜城王奚斤，自長安追擊赫連昌，至于安定，頡為監軍侍御史。

translations.literal: Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin, from Chang'an pursued Helian Chang to Anding; Jie was Supervisory Army Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin pursued Helian Chang from Chang'an as far as Anding; Jie served as Supervisory Army Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 斤以馬多疫死，士眾乏糧，乃深壘自固。

translations.literal: Jin, because many horses died of plague and the soldiers lacked grain, then built deep fortifications to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Jin's horses had died of plague and his men were short of grain, so he dug in behind strong fortifications.

sentences.zh: 遣太僕丘堆等督租於民間，為昌所敗。

translations.literal: He sent Master of the Stud Qiu Dui and others to levy grain rent among the people; they were defeated by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Master of the Stud Qiu Dui and others to collect grain from the countryside, and Chang defeated them.

sentences.zh: 昌遂驕矜，日來侵掠，芻牧者不得出，士卒患之。

translations.literal: Chang then grew arrogant and haughty, coming daily to raid and plunder; those gathering fodder and tending herds could not go out, and the soldiers were distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang grew bold and came raiding every day; men could not even go out to cut fodder or tend herds, and the troops were desperate.

sentences.zh: 頡進計曰：「本奉詔誅賊，今乃退守窮城，若不為賊殺，當以法誅。

translations.literal: Jie advanced a plan, saying: "We originally received the edict to execute the bandit; now we retreat to defend this desperate city—if we are not killed by the bandit, we will be executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: Jie offered a plan: "We were ordered here to destroy the enemy, yet now we cower in this trapped city. If the bandits do not kill us, the law will.

sentences.zh: 進退安有生路？

translations.literal: In advance or retreat, where is any path to life?
translations.idiomatic: Whether we advance or retreat, where is there any way to live?

sentences.zh: 而王公諸將，晏然無謀，將何以報恩塞責。

translations.literal: Yet the princes, dukes, and generals sit at ease with no plan—how will we repay grace and fulfill duty?"
translations.idiomatic: And the princes and generals sit idle with no plan at all—how are we to repay the emperor's trust or answer for our duty?"

sentences.zh: 」斤曰：「今若出戰，則馬力不足，以步擊騎，終無捷理。

translations.literal: Jin said: "If we fight now, our horses' strength is insufficient; foot soldiers attacking cavalry, in the end there is no way to victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jin replied, "If we fight now our horses are too weak. Foot soldiers against cavalry can never win.

sentences.zh: 當須京師救騎至，然後步陳擊於內，騎兵襲其外。

translations.literal: We must wait for rescue cavalry from the capital to arrive, then infantry formations strike from within, and cavalry raid from outside.
translations.idiomatic: We must wait for relief cavalry from the capital, then let the infantry sally from inside while horsemen strike from without.

sentences.zh: 所謂萬全之計也。

translations.literal: This is what is called the plan of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: That is the only safe course."

sentences.zh: 」頡曰：「今猛寇遊逸於外，而吾等兵疲力屈，士有飢色，不一決戰，則死在旦夕，何救兵之可待也！

translations.literal: Jie said: "Now the fierce bandit roams outside, while we are troops weary and strength exhausted, the soldiers showing hunger—if we do not decide battle at once, death comes within the day; how can we wait for rescue troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "The enemy roams freely while our men are exhausted and hungry. If we do not fight now, we die tomorrow—what rescue can we wait for?"

sentences.zh: 等死，當戰死，寧可坐受困乎？

translations.literal: If we must die equally, let us die in battle—how can we sit and accept besiegement?"
translations.idiomatic: If we must die, let us die fighting. Will we sit here and be strangled to death?"

sentences.zh: 」斤猶以馬為辭。

translations.literal: Jin still used the horses as his excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still pleaded the lack of horses.

sentences.zh: 頡曰：「今兵雖無馬，但將帥所乘，足得二百騎。

translations.literal: Jie said: "Though our troops now lack horses, the mounts of the commanders alone would suffice for two hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "Our soldiers may have no horses, but the commanders' mounts alone would make two hundred cavalry.

sentences.zh: 頡請募壯勇出擊之，就不能破，可以折其銳。

translations.literal: Jie requested to recruit the brave and stalwart to sally out and attack them; even if they cannot break them, they can blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Let me gather the bravest men and strike out. Even if we cannot break them, we can dull their momentum.

sentences.zh: 且昌狷而無謀，每好挑戰，眾皆識之。

translations.literal: Moreover Chang is narrow-minded and without stratagem; he always loves to challenge battle, and all recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Chang is rash and witless; he loves to fight in person, and every man knows his face.

sentences.zh: 若伏兵奄擊，昌可擒也。

translations.literal: If we set ambush and suddenly strike, Chang can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Set an ambush and strike suddenly, and Chang can be taken."

sentences.zh: 」斤猶難之。

translations.literal: Jin still found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 頡乃陰與尉眷等謀，選騎待焉。

translations.literal: Jie then secretly plotted with Wei Juan and others, selected cavalry and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then secretly conspired with Wei Juan and the others, picked out cavalry, and waited.

sentences.zh: 昌來攻壘，頡出應之。

translations.literal: Chang came to attack the fortifications; Jie went out to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang came to assault the camp, Jie rode out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 昌於陳前自接戰，軍士識昌，爭往赴之。

translations.literal: Chang personally engaged in battle before the formations; the soldiers recognized Chang and vied to rush toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang fought in person at the front of his line; the soldiers knew him and surged forward to reach him.

sentences.zh: 會天大風揚塵，晝昏，眾亂，昌退。

translations.literal: It happened that a great wind arose raising dust; day turned dim, the masses were in disorder, and Chang retreated.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind blew up dust and darkened the day; the ranks broke in confusion and Chang fell back.

sentences.zh: 頡等追擊，昌馬蹶而墜。

translations.literal: Jie and others pursued; Chang's horse stumbled and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and the others pursued; Chang's horse stumbled and threw him.

sentences.zh: 頡擒昌，送於京師。

translations.literal: Jie captured Chang and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jie seized Chang and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世祖大悅，拜頡建節將軍，賜爵西平公，代堆統攝諸軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was greatly pleased, appointing Jie General Who Establishes the Standard, granting the title Duke of Xiping, replacing Qiu Dui to command the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was delighted. He made Jie General Who Establishes the Standard, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xiping, and put him in command of the armies in place of Qiu Dui.

sentences.zh: 斤耻功不在己，輕追昌弟定於平涼，敗績。

translations.literal: Jin, ashamed that the merit was not his own, lightly pursued Chang's younger brother Ding at Pingliang and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that the credit was not his, Jin rashly pursued Chang's brother Ding to Pingliang and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 定將復入長安，詔頡鎮蒲坂以拒之。

translations.literal: Ding was about to re-enter Chang'an; an edict ordered Jie to garrison Puban to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding was about to re-enter Chang'an, an edict sent Jie to hold Puban and block him.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆遣將到彥之率眾寇河南，以援赫連定。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong sent the general Dao Yanzhi leading troops to invade Henan, to aid Helian Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent the general Dao Yanzhi with an army against Henan to relieve Helian Ding.

sentences.zh: 世祖以兵少，乃攝河南三鎮北渡。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, because his troops were few, withdrew the three garrisons of Henan north across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, with too few troops to hold the line, pulled the three Henan garrisons back north of the river.

sentences.zh: 彥之遂列守南岸，至于衡關。

translations.literal: Yanzhi then arrayed garrisons along the south bank, reaching Heng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi then spread his forces along the south bank as far as Heng Pass.

sentences.zh: [6]世祖西征赫連定。

translations.literal: [6] Emperor Shizu marched west against Helian Ding.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Emperor Shizu marched west to campaign against Helian Ding.

sentences.zh: 以頡為冠軍將軍，督諸軍擊彥之。

translations.literal: Jie was made General of Champion Cavalry and directed the armies to strike Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was appointed General of Champion Cavalry and put in command of the forces sent against Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 彥之遣將姚縱夫渡河攻冶坂，頡督諸軍擊之，斬首三千餘級，投水者甚眾。

translations.literal: Yanzhi sent the general Yu Zongfu to cross the river and attack Yebane; Jie directed the armies to strike them, beheading more than three thousand, and very many drowned themselves in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi sent the general Yu Zongfu across the river to attack Yebane; Jie routed them, taking more than three thousand heads, while many others drowned trying to escape.

sentences.zh: 遂濟河，攻洛陽，拔之，擒義隆將二十餘人，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river, attacked Luoyang, took it, captured more than twenty of Yilong's generals, and beheaded five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the river, stormed Luoyang, and took the city, capturing more than twenty of Yilong's officers and slaying five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 進攻虎牢，虎牢潰，義隆司州刺史尹沖墜城死。

translations.literal: He pressed the attack on Hulao; Hulao collapsed, and Yilong's Inspector of Si Province Yin Chong fell from the wall and died.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Hulao; the fortress fell, and Yilong's Inspector of Si Province Yin Chong plunged from the wall to his death.

sentences.zh: 又與琅邪王司馬楚之平滑臺，擒義隆將朱脩之、李元德及東郡太守申謨，俘獲萬餘人。

translations.literal: He also together with Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi pacified Pingtai, capturing Yilong's generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande, as well as Administrator of Dong Commandery Shen Mo, and taking more than ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi he also took Pingtai, capturing Yilong's generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande, Dong Commandery Administrator Shen Mo, and more than ten thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 乃振旅還京師。

translations.literal: He then rested the troops and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched his army home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 神䴥四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shengui he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Shengui.

sentences.zh: 贈征南大將軍、儀同三司，進爵為王，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Great General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Three Offices; advanced in rank to king; posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Great General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Three Offices, raised to princely rank, and given the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 頡為將，善綏士眾，及卒，義隆士卒降者，無不歎惜。

translations.literal: Jie as a general was skilled at pacifying soldiers and masses; when he died, all among Yilong's surrendered troops sighed in regret without exception.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Jie knew how to win men's hearts; when he died, even the Song soldiers who had surrendered to Wei mourned him.

sentences.zh: 同弟䐗，太宗時為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Tong's younger brother Xie, in Emperor Taizong's time was Administrator of Leiling.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's younger brother Xie served as Administrator of Leiling under Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 長子國，位至冠軍將軍，賜爵北平侯，杏城鎮將。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guo reached the rank of General of Champion Cavalry, was granted the title Marquis of Beiping, and was garrison commander of Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guo rose to General of Champion Cavalry, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Beiping, and served as garrison commander of Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 國弟難，有巧思。

translations.literal: Guo's younger brother Nan had ingenious ideas.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's younger brother Nan was a man of ingenious design.

sentences.zh: 陽平王杜超督諸將擊劉義隆，難參征南軍事，以功表為清河太守。

translations.literal: Prince of Yangping Du Chao directed the generals to strike Liu Yilong; Nan participated in southern campaign military affairs; for merit he was nominated as Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yangping Du Chao led the generals against Liu Yilong, Nan served on the southern campaign staff and, for his service, was recommended for Administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，諸將頻征和龍，皆以難為長史。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizu's time, whenever generals frequently campaigned against Helong, Nan was always made Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, whenever the generals marched repeatedly against Helong, Nan was always appointed chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 鑿山堙谷，省力兼功。

translations.literal: He cut through mountains and filled valleys, saving labor while doubling efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: He cut roads through mountains and filled ravines, saving labor while accomplishing twice the work.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 從駕南征，造浮橋於河，以功賜爵清河子。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial campaign south, built floating bridges on the river, and for merit was granted the title Viscount of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he accompanied the emperor, built floating bridges across the river, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe for his service.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子平城，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Pingcheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pingcheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 官至虞曹令。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Director of Forestry and Parks.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Director of Forestry and Parks.

sentences.zh: 為乙渾所殺。

translations.literal: He was killed by Yihun.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by Yihun.

sentences.zh: 子真，襲，降爵為公。

translations.literal: His son Zhen inherited, with title reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited the family rank, which was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 從世祖征伐有功，官至散騎常侍、尚書、安北將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Shizu's campaigns with merit, reaching the offices of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Master of Writing, and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Emperor Shizu and earned distinction, rising to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Master of Writing, and General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 徙為湘東公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Duke of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Duke of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 從征涼州，還，卒於路。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liangzhou; returning, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Liangzhou and died on the march home.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子干，襲，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: His son Gan inherited, with title reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gan inherited, with the rank reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 真次弟大拔，歷位尚書、散騎常侍、征西將軍，賜爵永平侯。

translations.literal: Zhen's next younger brother Daba held successive posts as Master of Writing, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and General Who Conquers the West, and was granted the title Marquis of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's next younger brother Daba served as Master of Writing, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and General Who Conquers the West in turn, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，為中都大官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was Director of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was made Director of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平東將軍、定州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ding Province; posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ding Province, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 子禀，字法生，襲。

translations.literal: His son Bin, styled Fasheng, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin, styled Fasheng, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 拜太子宮門大夫，稍遷趙郡太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Gate Grandee of the Crown Prince, then gradually promoted to Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Gate Grandee of the Crown Prince and later rose to Administrator of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 更滿還京，除冠軍將軍、城門校尉。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital, appointed General of Champion Cavalry and Commandant of the City Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to the capital and was made General of Champion Cavalry and Commandant of the City Gates.

sentences.zh: 出為征虜將軍、平城鎮將。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Captures the Barbarians and garrison commander of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Captures the Barbarians and garrison commander of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 遷朔州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Shuo Province, keeping his generalship.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Shuo Province while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 入為衞尉少卿。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as Vice Director of the Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Vice Director of the Guard Command.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 子貴宗，武定中，伏波將軍、開府水曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Guizong, in the Wuding era, was General Who Subdues the Waves and Staff Officer for Water Affairs in an open office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guizong, in the Wuding era, served as General Who Subdues the Waves and Staff Officer for Water Affairs at an open headquarters.

sentences.zh: 伏連兄孫安文。

translations.literal: Anwen, grandson of Fulan's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Anwen was a grandson of Fulan's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 從征平涼有功，賜爵覇城男，加虎威將軍。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Pingliang, for merit he was granted the title Viscount of Bacheng and additionally named General of Tiger Might.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Pingliang and for his service was enfeoffed as Viscount of Bacheng and made General of Tiger Might.

sentences.zh: 後遷三郎幢將。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Chief of the Third Lang Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made chief of the Third Lang Regiment.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，以其子毅貴，追贈安東將軍、冀州刺史、陽平公，諡曰定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign, because his son Yi was esteemed, [Anwen was] posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Ji Province, and Duke of Yangping, with posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gaozu's reign, because his son Yi was highly regarded, Anwen was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Yangping, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 毅，歷位內外，稍遷殿中尚書、散騎常侍，賜爵常山公，加安南將軍。

translations.literal: Yi held posts inside and outside [court], was gradually promoted to Master of Writing within the Palace, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, granted the title Duke of Changshan, and additionally named General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served at court and in the provinces in turn, rising to Master of Writing within the Palace and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan, and made General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以擒反人梁眾保，加侍中，本官如故。

translations.literal: Because he captured the rebel Liang Zhongbao, he was additionally named Palace Attendant; his original office was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing the rebel Liang Zhongbao he was made Palace Attendant while keeping his existing post.

sentences.zh: 後例降為侯。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent, [his title] was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following precedent, his rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 出除使持節、鎮東將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out [appointed] with the Staff of Authority as General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Ding Province with the Staff of Authority and the title General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 時太極殿成，將行考室之禮，引集羣臣，而雪不克饗。

translations.literal: At that time the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was completed; about to perform the kaoshi ceremony, [the emperor] gathered the officials, but snow prevented the feast.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was finished and the kaoshi rite was about to be performed, the emperor summoned his ministers—but snow made the feast impossible.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朕經始正殿，功構初成，將集百僚，考行大禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "I began and undertook the main hall; the work of construction is newly completed; I intend to gather the hundred officials and perform the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "I have built the main hall from the ground up, and the work is newly finished. I mean to gather all my ministers and perform the great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 然同雲仍結，霏雪驟零，將由寡昧，未能仰答天心。

translations.literal: Yet the same clouds still gather, fine snow suddenly falls—perhaps because of my dullness, I cannot look up and respond to Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the clouds still mass and fine snow falls suddenly. Perhaps my own dullness keeps me from answering Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 此之不德，咎竟焉在？

translations.literal: This lack of virtue—where does the blame ultimately lie?
translations.idiomatic: Where does the fault lie for this want of virtue?

sentences.zh: 卿等宜各陳所懷，以匡不逮。

translations.literal: You should each state what is in your hearts to aid my deficiencies.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you should speak your mind and help me mend what I lack.

sentences.zh: 」毅稽首對曰：「雪霜風雨，天地之常；

translations.literal: " Yi prostrated himself and replied: "Snow, frost, wind, and rain are the constant ways of Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: " Yi kowtowed and answered, "Snow, frost, wind, and rain are Heaven and Earth's ordinary course;

sentences.zh: 夏霂冬霰，四時恒節。

translations.literal: Summer rain and winter hail are the regular seasons of the four times.
translations.idiomatic: summer showers and winter sleet belong to the fixed cycle of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 今隆冬雪降，固是其時。

translations.literal: Now in deep winter snow falls—this is surely its proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Snow in the depths of winter is exactly what one should expect.

sentences.zh: 又禮云：『雨沾服失容，則廢』，禮自古而然，不足為異。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rites say: 'When rain soaks the garments and disfigures appearance, then cancel.' Ritual has been thus since antiquity; it is not enough to count as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Rites say, 'If rain soaks the robes and mars one's appearance, the rite is canceled.' That has been the rule since antiquity and is nothing out of the ordinary."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「昔劉秀將濟，呼沱為之冰合。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said: "In the past Liu Xiu was about to cross, and the Hutuo froze solid for him.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu said, "When Liu Xiu was about to cross the river, the Hutuo froze over for him.

sentences.zh: 但朕德謝古人，不能仰感天意故也。」

translations.literal: But my virtue falls short of the ancients—I cannot look up and move Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: My virtue falls short of the ancients', and I cannot move Heaven as they did."

sentences.zh: 後轉都督涼河二州、鄯善鎮諸軍事，涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to oversee military affairs of the two provinces Liang and He and of Zhashan Garrison, and was Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made overseer of military affairs in Liang and He provinces and at Zhashan Garrison, and Inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，毅表諫曰：「伏承六軍雲動，問罪荊揚，弔民淮表，一同甌越。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south, Yi submitted a memorial remonstrating: "I humbly learn the six armies move like clouds, to call to account Jing and Yang, to console the people east of the Huai, all as one with Ou and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Yi submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I humbly hear that the six armies are on the move, to punish Jing and Yang, succor the people beyond the Huai, and unite the land as once with Ou and Yue.

sentences.zh: 但臣愚見，私竊未安。

translations.literal: But this subject's foolish view privately cannot feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my foolish view I cannot privately feel at ease.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 京邑新遷，百姓易業，公私草創，生途索然。

translations.literal: The capital was newly moved; the people changed their occupations; public and private affairs were freshly begun; the path of livelihood was bleak.
translations.idiomatic: The capital has only just been moved; the people are still changing trades; public and private life are still being built from nothing; livelihood is thin everywhere.

sentences.zh: 兼往歲弗稔，民多飢饉，二三之際，嗟惋易興。

translations.literal: Moreover last year did not yield well; many among the people faced famine; among common folk, sighing and regret easily arise.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the last harvest was poor and many people are hungry; among ordinary folk, sighs and resentment come easily.

sentences.zh: 天道悠長，宜遵養時晦，願抑赫斯，以待後日。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven is long; one should follow 'nourish one's strength and bide one's time'; I wish to restrain furious display and await a later day.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's course is long. It is fitting to hide one's strength and wait for the right moment. I beg you to hold back your wrath and leave the campaign for another day."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「時不自來，因人則合。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "The opportune moment does not come of itself; it comes together through people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "The right moment does not arrive on its own; it comes when men make it so.

sentences.zh: 今年人事，殊非昔歲。

translations.literal: This year's affairs of men are quite unlike last year.
translations.idiomatic: This year's circumstances are nothing like last year's.

sentences.zh: 守株之唱，便可停也。

translations.literal: The song of waiting by the stump may stop.
translations.idiomatic: Leave off the counsel of one who waits by a tree stump for a rabbit.

sentences.zh: 陽九利涉，豈卿所知也。」

translations.literal: Crossing the Yang Nine brings benefit—how could you know?"
translations.idiomatic: In the Yang Nine year one must cross the waters—how could you understand that?"

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-first year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 賜錢二十萬，布二百匹。

translations.literal: He was given two hundred thousand coins and two hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted two hundred thousand coins and two hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 丘堆，代人也，美容儀，以忠謹親侍。

translations.literal: Qiu Dui, a man of Dai, had handsome bearing; because of loyalty and diligence he attended closely.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Dui was a man of Dai, handsome in appearance, who served at close hand because of his loyalty and diligence.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，拾遺左右，稍遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, [he served as] remonstrator at the emperor's side, gradually promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, Dui served as remonstrator at his side and was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 與叔孫建等討滅山胡。

translations.literal: Together with Shusun Jian and others he campaigned to destroy the Shanhu.
translations.idiomatic: With Shusun Jian and others he campaigned against the Shanhu and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 劉裕泝河西伐，詔堆與建自河內次枋頭以備寇盜。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu marched west along the Yellow River, an edict ordered Dui and Jian from Henei to encamp at Fangtou against raiders.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched west along the Yellow River, an edict ordered Dui and Jian to move from Henei and encamp at Fangtou against raiders.

sentences.zh: 姚泓既滅，堆留鎮并州。

translations.literal: After Yao Hong was destroyed, Dui remained to garrison Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Hong was destroyed, Dui stayed behind to garrison Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 赫連屈孑遣三千騎寇河西，堆自并州與游擊將軍王洛生擊走之。

translations.literal: Helian Qujie sent three thousand cavalry to raid Hexi; Dui from Bing Province with Mobile General Wang Luosheng struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Qujie sent three thousand cavalry to raid Hexi; Dui marched from Bing Province with Mobile General Wang Luosheng and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵為侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title of marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 世祖監國臨朝，堆與太尉穆觀等為右弼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu as crown prince presided at court, Dui with Grand Commandant Mu Guan and others were right assistants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu as crown prince held court, Dui and Grand Commandant Mu Guan and others served as his right-hand counselors.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進爵臨淮公，加鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, [Dui] was advanced to Duke of Linhuai and additionally named General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu came to the throne, Dui was raised to Duke of Linhuai and made General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 徙為太僕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 世祖征赫連昌，堆與常山王素督步兵三萬人為後繼。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang; Dui with Prince of Changshan Su commanded thirty thousand infantry as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu marched against Helian Chang, Dui and Prince of Changshan Su led thirty thousand foot soldiers as the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 昌戰敗南奔，世祖遣堆與宗正娥清率五千騎略地關右。

translations.literal: Chang was defeated and fled south; Emperor Shizu sent Dui with Chief of the Imperial Clan E Qing at the head of five thousand cavalry to raid the lands west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was defeated and fled south; Emperor Shizu sent Dui and Chief of the Imperial Clan E Qing with five thousand cavalry to raid the territory west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 昌貳城守將堅守不下，堆與清攻拔之。

translations.literal: Chang's garrison commander at Ercheng held firm and would not yield; Dui and Qing attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's garrison commander at Ercheng held out stubbornly; Dui and Qing attacked and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 詔堆班師，宜城王奚斤表留堆等進平昌，許之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dui to withdraw the army; Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin memorialized to keep Dui and others to advance and pacify Chang; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Dui to withdraw, but Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin memorialized asking that Dui and the others remain to finish off Chang; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 堆、斤合軍與昌相拒擊。

translations.literal: Dui and Jin joined armies and faced Chang in combat.
translations.idiomatic: Dui and Jin united their forces and fought Chang.

sentences.zh: 士馬乏糧，堆與義兵將軍封禮督租於民間，士卒暴掠，為昌所襲，敗績。

translations.literal: Horses and soldiers lacked grain; Dui with Righteous Troops General Feng Li supervised tax collection among the people; soldiers plundered violently; they were struck by Chang and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: With horses and men short of grain, Dui and Righteous Troops General Feng Li went among the people to levy supplies; the soldiers looted freely, Chang struck them, and they were routed.

sentences.zh: 堆將數百騎還城。

translations.literal: Dui led several hundred cavalry back to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Dui escaped with a few hundred cavalry back to the city.

sentences.zh: 斤追擊赫連定，留堆守輜重。

translations.literal: Jin pursued Helian Ding, leaving Dui to guard the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pursued Helian Ding and left Dui to guard the baggage train.

sentences.zh: 斤為定所擒，堆聞而棄甲走長安，復將高涼王禮棄守東走蒲坂。

translations.literal: Jin was captured by Ding; hearing this Dui cast off armor and fled to Chang'an, then again with Prince of Gaoliang Li abandoned the garrison and fled east to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was captured by Ding; when Dui heard of it he threw off his armor and fled to Chang'an, then with Prince of Gaoliang Li abandoned the garrison and fled east to Puban.

sentences.zh: 世祖大怒，遣西平公安頡斬堆。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was greatly angered; he sent Prince of Xiping An Jie to execute Dui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was furious and sent Prince of Xiping An Jie to execute Dui.

sentences.zh: 延和初，詔曰：「堆，國之肺腑，勳著先朝，西征喪師，遂從軍法。

translations.literal: Early in Yanhe, an edict said: "Dui was the state's inner flesh, his merit outstanding in the former reign; the western expedition lost the army, and thus he suffered military law.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yanhe an edict said, "Dui was kin to the throne and his merit shone in the previous reign, but the western campaign lost the army and he paid under military law.

sentences.zh: 國除祀絕，朕甚愍之。

translations.literal: The state was extinguished and sacrifices cut off—I deeply pity this.
translations.idiomatic: His line was extinguished and his sacrifices ended, and I deeply pity it.

sentences.zh: 可賜其子跋爵淮陵侯，加安遠將軍。

translations.literal: His son Ba may be granted the title Marquis of Huailing and additionally named General Who Pacifies the Remote.
translations.idiomatic: Let his son Ba be granted the title Marquis of Huailing and made General Who Pacifies the Remote."

sentences.zh: 」後征蓋吳，戰沒。

translations.literal: Later, campaigning against Gai Wu, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against Gai Wu, he was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 子麟，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Lin inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 歷位駕部令。

translations.literal: He held successive posts reaching Director of the Imperial Chariot Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Director of the Imperial Chariot Office.

sentences.zh: 出為瑕丘鎮將、假平南將軍、東海公。

translations.literal: He was sent out as garrison commander of Xiqiu, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and Duke of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as garrison commander of Xiqiu, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 遷東兗州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Eastern Yan Province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Inspector of Eastern Yan Province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 娥清，代人也。

translations.literal: E Qing, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: E Qing was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有將略，累著戰功。

translations.literal: From youth he had military talent; repeatedly he distinguished himself in battle.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed military talent and won distinction again and again in battle.

sentences.zh: 稍遷振威將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General Who Quells Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to General Who Quells Might.

sentences.zh: 劉裕遣將朱超石寇平原，至畔城遁還。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent General Zhu Chaoshi to raid Pingyuan; reaching Pancheng he fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent General Zhu Chaoshi to raid Pingyuan, but Chaoshi turned back after reaching Pancheng.

sentences.zh: 清與長孫道生追之，至河，獲其將楊豐。

translations.literal: Qing with Zhangsun Daosheng pursued them; reaching the river, they captured their general Yang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Zhangsun Daosheng pursued them, and at the river captured their general Yang Feng.

sentences.zh: 還，拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Returning, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 先是，徒河民散居三州，頗為民害。

translations.literal: Before this, the people of Tuhe scattered through three provinces were quite a harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tuhe people scattered across three provinces had become a serious nuisance to the local population.

sentences.zh: 詔清徙之平城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qing to relocate them to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qing to relocate them to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 清善綏撫，徙者如歸。

translations.literal: Qing was good at comforting; those relocated felt as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Qing handled the resettlement with skill, and the migrants felt as though they were coming home.

sentences.zh: 太宗南巡幸鄴，以清為中領軍將軍，與宋兵將軍周幾等渡河略地。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong on a southern tour visited Ye; Qing was made General of the Central Guard Army; with General of Song Troops Zhou Ji and others he crossed the river to raid territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong toured the south and visited Ye, Qing was made General of the Central Guard Army and, with General of Song Troops Zhou Ji and others, crossed the river to seize territory.

sentences.zh: 至湖陸，高平民屯聚林藪，拒射官軍，清等因誅數千家，虜獲萬餘口。
