translations.literal: Reaching Hulu, the people of Gaoping gathered in forests and marshes, resisted and shot at the official army; Qing and others thereupon executed several thousand households and captured over ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: At Hulu, Gaoping people had gathered in woods and marshes and fired on the imperial troops; Qing and his men executed several thousand households and took more than ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 賜爵須昌侯。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 清與幾等遂鎮枋頭。

translations.literal: Qing with Ji and others then garrisoned Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, Ji, and the others then garrisoned Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，清自枋頭還京師，假征南將軍，進為東平公。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign, Qing from Fangtou returned to the capital; acting General Who Conquers the South; advanced to Duke of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign Qing returned from Fangtou to the capital, was made acting General Who Conquers the South, and was raised to Duke of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕大檀徙居漠南，清與平陽王長孫翰從東道出長川討之，大獲而還。

translations.literal: Datan of the Rouran moved to south of the desert; Qing with Prince of Pingyang Zhangsun Han from the eastern route via Changchuan attacked them; they gained greatly and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Datan of the Rouran moved south of the desert, Qing and Prince of Pingyang Zhangsun Han marched east through Changchuan to attack him, took a great haul, and returned.

sentences.zh: 轉宗正卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 尋從征蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the campaign against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined the campaign against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 又從平統萬，遂與奚斤追赫連昌至安定，與昌相持。

translations.literal: He also followed the pacification of Tongwan; then with Xi Jin pursued Helian Chang to Anding and faced him in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the capture of Tongwan, then with Xi Jin pursued Helian Chang to Anding and locked horns with him.

sentences.zh: 及安頡擒昌，昌弟定西走，斤追之。

translations.literal: When An Jie captured Chang, Chang's brother Ding fled west; Jin pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Jie captured Chang, Chang's brother Ding fled west and Jin pursued him.

sentences.zh: 清欲尋水而往，斤不從，遂與斤俱為定所擒。

translations.literal: Qing wished to follow water and go; Jin would not agree; thus both were captured by Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Qing wanted to march along the waterways, but Jin refused; in the end both were captured by Ding.

sentences.zh: 世祖克平涼，乃得還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took Pingliang, they were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu took Pingliang, they were freed and returned.

sentences.zh: 後詔清鎮并州，討山胡白龍於西河，斬白龍父及其將帥，遂屠其城。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered Qing to garrison Bing Province; he campaigned against the Shanhu rebel Bai Long in Xihe; beheaded Bai Long's father and his commanders; then slaughtered their city.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict posted Qing to garrison Bing Province; he campaigned against the Shanhu rebel Bai Long in Xihe, beheaded Bai Long's father and his commanders, and then slaughtered the city.

sentences.zh: 遷平東將軍，與古弼等東討馮文通。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East; with Gu Bi and others he campaigned east against Feng Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and, with Gu Bi and others, marched east against Feng Wentong.

sentences.zh: 以不急戰，文通奔高麗，檻車徵，黜為門卒。

translations.literal: Because he did not press the battle, Wentong fled to Goryeo; [Qing was] summoned in a caged cart and demoted to gate soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Because he did not press the attack, Wentong fled to Goryeo; Qing was summoned back in a caged cart and reduced to gate soldier.

sentences.zh: 遂卒於家。

translations.literal: Then he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home soon after.

sentences.zh: 子延，官至員外散騎常侍，賜爵南平公。

translations.literal: His son Yan reached the office of Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; granted the title Duke of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan rose to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 劉尼，代人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ni, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 本姓獨孤氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Dugu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖敦，有功於太祖，為方面大人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dun had merit with Emperor Taizu; he was a regional great chief.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dun had served Emperor Taizu with distinction and held the rank of regional great chief.

sentences.zh: 父婁，冠軍將軍，卒贈并州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Lou was General of Champion Cavalry; at death posthumously awarded Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lou was General of Champion Cavalry and was posthumously made Inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 尼少壯健，有膂力，勇果善射，世祖見而善之，拜羽林中郎，賜爵昌國子，加振威將軍。

translations.literal: Ni from youth was robust and strong, had physical strength, was brave and decisive and skilled at archery; Emperor Shizu saw him and favored him; appointed Gentleman in the Feathered Forest Guard; granted the title Viscount of Changguo; added General Who Quells Might.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was strong and vigorous from youth, brave and skilled with the bow; Emperor Shizu took a liking to him, made him Gentleman in the Feathered Forest Guard, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Changguo, and named him General Who Quells Might.

sentences.zh: 宗愛既殺南安王余於東廟，祕之，惟尼知狀。

translations.literal: After Zong Ai had killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the Eastern Temple, he kept it secret; only Ni knew the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the Eastern Temple he kept it secret; only Ni knew what had happened.

sentences.zh: 尼勸愛立高宗。

translations.literal: Ni urged Ai to install Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Ni urged Ai to put Emperor Gaozong on the throne.

sentences.zh: 愛自以負罪於景穆，聞而驚曰：「君大癡人，皇孫若立，豈忘正平時事乎？

translations.literal: Ai felt himself guilty toward Jingmu; on hearing this he was alarmed and said: "You great fool—if the imperial grandson is installed, will he not remember the Zhengping-era affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Ai knew himself guilty toward Crown Prince Jingmu; when he heard this he was alarmed and said, "You great fool—if the imperial grandson takes the throne, will he not remember what happened in the Zhengping era?

sentences.zh: 」尼曰：「若爾，今欲立誰？

translations.literal: " Ni said: "If so, whom do you wish to install now?
translations.idiomatic: " Ni said, "If so, whom do you mean to install now?

sentences.zh: 」愛曰：「待還宮，擢諸王子賢者而立之。

translations.literal: " Ai said: "When we return to the palace, I will select a worthy one among the princes and install him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ai said, "When we return to the palace, I will choose a worthy prince and put him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 」尼懼其有變，密以狀告殿中尚書源賀，賀時與尼俱典兵宿衞。

translations.literal: " Ni feared he would change his mind; secretly he reported the situation to Palace Master of Writing Yuan He; He at the time with Ni jointly commanded troops on night guard.
translations.idiomatic: " Ni feared Ai would change course; secretly he told Palace Master of Writing Yuan He what had happened. He was then serving with Ni in command of the night guard.

sentences.zh: 仍共南部尚書陸麗謀曰：「宗愛既立南安，還復殺之。

translations.literal: He then together with Master of Writing of the Southern Department Lu Li schemed, saying: "Zong Ai after installing Nan'an again killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then met with Master of Writing of the Southern Department Lu Li and said, "Zong Ai installed Nan'an and then killed him again.

sentences.zh: 今不能奉戴皇孫，以順民望，社稷危矣。

translations.literal: Now if we cannot install the imperial grandson to accord with the people's hopes, the altars of state are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not install the imperial grandson now and answer the people's hopes, the altars of state are in peril.

sentences.zh: 將欲如何？

translations.literal: What are we to do?
translations.idiomatic: What are we to do?

sentences.zh: 」麗曰：「唯有密奉皇孫耳。

translations.literal: " Li said: "Only to secretly install the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: " Li said, "We must secretly install the imperial grandson."

sentences.zh: 」於是賀與尚書長孫渴侯嚴兵守衞，尼與麗迎高宗於苑中。

translations.literal: " Thereupon He together with Master of Writing Zhangsun Kehou mustered troops and kept guard; Ni and Li welcomed Emperor Gaozong in the park.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon He and Master of Writing Zhangsun Kehou drew up troops and stood guard, while Ni and Li brought Emperor Gaozong out from the park.

sentences.zh: 麗抱高宗於馬上，入京城。

translations.literal: Li held Emperor Gaozong on the horse and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li held Emperor Gaozong in the saddle and rode into the capital.

sentences.zh: 尼馳還東廟，大呼曰：「宗愛殺南安王，大逆不道。

translations.literal: Ni galloped back to the Eastern Temple and shouted loudly: "Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an—great treason and unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ni galloped back to the Eastern Temple and cried out, "Zong Ai has killed Prince of Nan'an—treason of the worst kind.

sentences.zh: 皇孫已登大位，有詔，宿衞之士皆可還宮。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson has already ascended the great throne. There is an edict: night-guard soldiers may all return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson has already ascended the throne. By edict, all night-guard soldiers may return to the palace."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸唱萬歲。

translations.literal: " All together cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: All cried "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 賀及渴侯登執宗愛、賈周等，勒兵而入，奉高宗於宮門外，入登永安殿。

translations.literal: He and Kehou Deng seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and others; leading troops they entered, presented Emperor Gaozong outside the palace gates, and entered to ascend Yong'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He and Kehou Deng seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and the rest; they led their troops inside, presented Emperor Gaozong at the palace gates, and brought him in to ascend Yong'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 以尼為內行長，進爵建昌侯。

translations.literal: Ni was made Chief of the Inner Guard and advanced to Marquis of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was made Chief of the Inner Guard and raised to Marquis of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、安南將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 又進爵東安公。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to Duke of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was further raised to Duke of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書右僕射，加侍中，進封為王。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, added Palace Attendant, and advanced to enfeoffment as king.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as king.

sentences.zh: 子社生，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son She Sheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son She Sheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，寧朔將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he was General of Ning Shuo and Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he served as General of Ning Shuo and Colonel of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 熙平初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the start of the Xiping era.

sentences.zh: 贈龍驤將軍、朔州刺史，諡曰克。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Shuo Province; posthumous name Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Shuo Province, with the posthumous name Ke.

sentences.zh: 劉尼，代人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ni, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 本姓獨孤氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Dugu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖敦，有功於太祖，為方面大人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dun had merit with Emperor Taizu; he was a regional great chief.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dun had served Emperor Taizu with distinction and held the rank of regional great chief.

sentences.zh: 父婁，冠軍將軍，卒贈并州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Lou was General of Champion Cavalry; at death posthumously awarded Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lou was General of Champion Cavalry and was posthumously made Inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 尼少壯健，有膂力，勇果善射，世祖見而善之，拜羽林中郎，賜爵昌國子，加振威將軍。

translations.literal: Ni from youth was robust and strong, had physical strength, was brave and decisive and skilled at archery; Emperor Shizu saw him and favored him; appointed Gentleman in the Feathered Forest Guard; granted the title Viscount of Changguo; added General Who Quells Might.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was strong and vigorous from youth, brave and skilled with the bow; Emperor Shizu took a liking to him, made him Gentleman in the Feathered Forest Guard, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Changguo, and named him General Who Quells Might.

sentences.zh: 宗愛既殺南安王余於東廟，祕之，惟尼知狀。

translations.literal: After Zong Ai had killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the Eastern Temple, he kept it secret; only Ni knew the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an Yu at the Eastern Temple he kept it secret; only Ni knew what had happened.

sentences.zh: 尼勸愛立高宗。

translations.literal: Ni urged Ai to install Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Ni urged Ai to put Emperor Gaozong on the throne.

sentences.zh: 愛自以負罪於景穆，聞而驚曰：「君大癡人，皇孫若立，豈忘正平時事乎？

translations.literal: Ai felt himself guilty toward Jingmu; on hearing this he was alarmed and said: "You great fool—if the imperial grandson is installed, will he not remember the Zhengping-era affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Ai knew himself guilty toward Crown Prince Jingmu; when he heard this he was alarmed and said, "You great fool—if the imperial grandson takes the throne, will he not remember what happened in the Zhengping era?

sentences.zh: 」尼曰：「若爾，今欲立誰？

translations.literal: " Ni said: "If so, whom do you wish to install now?
translations.idiomatic: " Ni said, "If so, whom do you mean to install now?

sentences.zh: 」愛曰：「待還宮，擢諸王子賢者而立之。

translations.literal: " Ai said: "When we return to the palace, I will select a worthy one among the princes and install him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ai said, "When we return to the palace, I will choose a worthy prince and put him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 」尼懼其有變，密以狀告殿中尚書源賀，賀時與尼俱典兵宿衞。

translations.literal: " Ni feared he would change his mind; secretly he reported the situation to Palace Master of Writing Yuan He; He at the time with Ni jointly commanded troops on night guard.
translations.idiomatic: " Ni feared Ai would change course; secretly he told Palace Master of Writing Yuan He what had happened. He was then serving with Ni in command of the night guard.

sentences.zh: 仍共南部尚書陸麗謀曰：「宗愛既立南安，還復殺之。

translations.literal: He then together with Master of Writing of the Southern Department Lu Li schemed, saying: "Zong Ai after installing Nan'an again killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then met with Master of Writing of the Southern Department Lu Li and said, "Zong Ai installed Nan'an and then killed him again.

sentences.zh: 今不能奉戴皇孫，以順民望，社稷危矣。

translations.literal: Now if we cannot install the imperial grandson to accord with the people's hopes, the altars of state are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not install the imperial grandson now and answer the people's hopes, the altars of state are in peril.

sentences.zh: 將欲如何？

translations.literal: What are we to do?
translations.idiomatic: What are we to do?

sentences.zh: 」麗曰：「唯有密奉皇孫耳。

translations.literal: " Li said: "Only to secretly install the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: " Li said, "We must secretly install the imperial grandson."

sentences.zh: 」於是賀與尚書長孫渴侯嚴兵守衞，尼與麗迎高宗於苑中。

translations.literal: " Thereupon He together with Master of Writing Zhangsun Kehou mustered troops and kept guard; Ni and Li welcomed Emperor Gaozong in the park.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon He and Master of Writing Zhangsun Kehou drew up troops and stood guard, while Ni and Li brought Emperor Gaozong out from the park.

sentences.zh: 麗抱高宗於馬上，入京城。

translations.literal: Li held Emperor Gaozong on the horse and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li held Emperor Gaozong in the saddle and rode into the capital.

sentences.zh: 尼馳還東廟，大呼曰：「宗愛殺南安王，大逆不道。

translations.literal: Ni galloped back to the Eastern Temple and shouted loudly: "Zong Ai killed Prince of Nan'an—great treason and unrighteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ni galloped back to the Eastern Temple and cried out, "Zong Ai has killed Prince of Nan'an—treason of the worst kind.

sentences.zh: 皇孫已登大位，有詔，宿衞之士皆可還宮。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson has already ascended the great throne. There is an edict: night-guard soldiers may all return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson has already ascended the throne. By edict, all night-guard soldiers may return to the palace."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸唱萬歲。

translations.literal: " All together cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: All cried "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 賀及渴侯登執宗愛、賈周等，勒兵而入，奉高宗於宮門外，入登永安殿。

translations.literal: He and Kehou Deng seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and others; leading troops they entered, presented Emperor Gaozong outside the palace gates, and entered to ascend Yong'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He and Kehou Deng seized Zong Ai, Jia Zhou, and the rest; they led their troops inside, presented Emperor Gaozong at the palace gates, and brought him in to ascend Yong'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 以尼為內行長，進爵建昌侯。

translations.literal: Ni was made Chief of the Inner Guard and advanced to Marquis of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was made Chief of the Inner Guard and raised to Marquis of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、安南將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 又進爵東安公。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to Duke of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was further raised to Duke of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書右僕射，加侍中，進封為王。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, added Palace Attendant, and advanced to enfeoffment as king.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as king.

sentences.zh: 子社生，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son She Sheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son She Sheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，寧朔將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he was General of Ning Shuo and Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he served as General of Ning Shuo and Colonel of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 熙平初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the start of the Xiping era.

sentences.zh: 贈龍驤將軍、朔州刺史，諡曰克。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Shuo Province; posthumous name Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Shuo Province, with the posthumous name Ke.

sentences.zh: 奚眷，代人也。

translations.literal: Xi Juan, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Juan was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有將略。

translations.literal: From youth he had military talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed military talent.

sentences.zh: 太祖時有戰功。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizu's time he had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizu's reign he won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 太宗時為尚書、假安南將軍、虎牢鎮將，為寇所憚。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's time he was Master of Writing, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and garrison commander of Hulao; enemies feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he served as Master of Writing, acting General Who Pacifies the South, and commandant of Hulao—foes feared him.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，為中軍、都曹尚書，復鎮虎牢，賜爵南陽公，加使持節、侍中、都督豫洛二州河內諸軍事、鎮南將軍、開府。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign he was Central Army commander and Master of Writing of the Capital Office; again garrisoned Hulao; granted the title Duke of Nanyang; added Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Yu and Luo two provinces and Henei, General Who Guards the South, and an open office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign he was made Central Army commander and Master of Writing of the Capital Office, again garrisoned Hulao, enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang, and given the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, command of military affairs in Yu and Luo provinces and Henei, the title General Who Guards the South, and an open headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋徙鎮長安。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸美稷，眷受詔督諸軍，共討山胡白龍于西河，破之，屠其城，斬首數千級，虜其妻子而還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu visited Meiji, Juan received orders to command the armies jointly to campaign against the Shanhu Bai Long in Xihe; they broke him, slaughtered his city, severed heads in the thousands, captured his wife and children and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu visited Meiji, Juan was ordered to command the armies in a joint campaign against the Shanhu rebel Bai Long in Xihe; they routed him, slaughtered his city, took thousands of heads, and returned with his wife and children as captives.

sentences.zh: 世祖平姑臧，遣眷討沮渠牧犍弟私署張掖太守宜得。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Guzang, he sent Juan to campaign against Juqu Mujian's younger brother Yide, who had privately installed himself as Grand Administrator of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Guzang, he sent Juan against Juqu Mujian's younger brother Yide, who had set himself up as Grand Administrator of Zhangye without authorization.

sentences.zh: 宜得奔酒泉，酒泉太守無諱與宜得奔高昌。

translations.literal: Yide fled to Jiuquan; Jiuquan Grand Administrator Wuwei together with Yide fled to Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Yide fled to Jiuquan; Grand Administrator Wuwei of Jiuquan fled with him to Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 獲其二城。

translations.literal: [They] captured the two cities.
translations.idiomatic: They captured both cities.

sentences.zh: 後沮渠天周復據酒泉，眷討平之，虜男女四千餘人。

translations.literal: Later Juqu Tianzhou again held Jiuquan; Juan campaigned and pacified it, capturing over four thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Later Juqu Tianzhou seized Jiuquan again; Juan campaigned against him, pacified the city, and took more than four thousand men and women captive.

sentences.zh: 世祖征蠕蠕，以眷為尚書，督偏將出別道，詔會鹿渾海。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against the Rouran, Juan was made Master of Writing and commanded detached generals out by a separate route; an edict ordered rendezvous at Luhun Lake.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu marched against the Rouran, Juan was made Master of Writing and sent to lead detached generals by a separate route, with orders to rendezvous at Luhun Lake.

sentences.zh: 眷與中山王辰等諸大將俱後期，斬于都南。

translations.literal: Juan together with Prince of Zhongshan Chen and other great generals all arrived late; he was beheaded south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Juan, Prince of Zhongshan Chen, and the other great generals all arrived late; Juan was beheaded south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 爵除。

translations.literal: His title was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: His title was revoked.

sentences.zh: 車伊洛，焉耆胡也。

translations.literal: Che Yiluo was a man of the Yanqi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yiluo was a man of the Yanqi Hu.

sentences.zh: 世為東境部落帥，恒修職貢。

translations.literal: For generations his family were chieftains of eastern-border tribes; they constantly maintained tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been chieftains of eastern-border tribes, and they faithfully paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 世祖錄其誠款，延和中授伊洛平西將軍，封前部王，賜絹一百匹，綿一百斤，繡衣一具，金帶靴帽。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu recorded his sincerity; in Yanhe he invested Yiluo as General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed him as King of the Front Division, and granted a hundred bolts of silk, a hundred jin of cotton, one set of embroidered robes, and gold belt, boots, and cap.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu recognized his loyalty; in the Yanhe era he made Yiluo General Who Pacifies the West and King of the Front Division, granting him a hundred bolts of silk, a hundred jin of cotton, a set of embroidered robes, and a gold belt, boots, and cap.

sentences.zh: 伊洛大悅，規欲歸闕。

translations.literal: Yiluo was greatly pleased and planned to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo was overjoyed and planned to come to court.

sentences.zh: 沮渠無諱斷路，伊洛與無諱連戰，破之。

translations.literal: Juqu Wuwei cut the road; Yiluo fought Wuwei repeatedly and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Wuwei blocked the road; Yiluo fought him again and again and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 時無諱卒，其弟天周奪無諱子乾壽兵，規領部曲。

translations.literal: At that time Wuwei died; his younger brother Tianzhou seized the troops of Wuwei's son Qianshou and planned to take command of the tribal forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuwei died, his younger brother Tianzhou seized the troops of Wuwei's son Qianshou and meant to take command of the tribal forces.

sentences.zh: 伊洛前後遣使招喻，乾壽等率戶五百餘家來奔，伊洛送之京師。

translations.literal: Yiluo repeatedly sent envoys to summon and persuade; Qianshou and others led over five hundred households to defect; Yiluo sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo sent envoys again and again to win them over; Qianshou and others led more than five hundred households to defect, and Yiluo sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又招喻李寶弟欽等五十餘人，送詣敦煌。

translations.literal: He also persuaded Li Bao's younger brother Qin and over fifty others, and sent them to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He also won over Li Bao's younger brother Qin and more than fifty others and sent them to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 伊洛又率部眾二千餘人伐高昌，討破焉耆東關七城，虜獲男女二百人，駝千頭，馬千匹。

translations.literal: Yiluo again led over two thousand of his tribesmen to attack Gaochang; he campaigned and broke seven cities at the eastern pass of Yanqi, capturing two hundred men and women, a thousand camels, and a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo again led more than two thousand of his tribesmen against Gaochang, took seven cities at the eastern pass of Yanqi, and captured two hundred men and women, a thousand camels, and a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 以金一百斤奉獻。

translations.literal: He presented a hundred jin of gold as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a hundred jin of gold as tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，伊洛征焉耆，留其子歇守城，而安周乘虛引蠕蠕三道圍歇，并遣使謂歇曰：「爾父已投大魏，爾速歸首，當賜爾爵號。

translations.literal: Previously, when Yiluo campaigned in Yanqi, he left his son Xie to garrison the city; An Zhou seized the opportunity and led the Rouran in three columns to besiege Xie, also sending an envoy telling Xie: "Your father has already submitted to Great Wei; quickly surrender and you will be granted a title of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yiluo campaigned in Yanqi, he left his son Xie to hold the city. An Zhou seized the moment and led the Rouran in three columns to besiege Xie, also sending an envoy who said, "Your father has already submitted to Great Wei. Surrender at once and you will be granted a title.

sentences.zh: 」歇固守，連戰。

translations.literal: " Xie held firm and fought repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie held the city and fought on.

sentences.zh: 久之，外無救援，為安周所陷，走奔伊洛。

translations.literal: After a long while, with no relief from outside, he was overcome by An Zhou and fled to join Yiluo.
translations.idiomatic: After a long siege, with no relief from outside, he was overrun by An Zhou and fled to rejoin Yiluo.

sentences.zh: 伊洛收集遺散一千餘家，歸焉耆鎮。

translations.literal: Yiluo gathered over a thousand scattered households and returned to the Yanqi garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo gathered more than a thousand scattered households and returned to the Yanqi garrison.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu commended him.

sentences.zh: 正平元年，詔伊洛曰：「歇年尚幼，能固守城邑，忠節顯著，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengping, an edict to Yiluo said: "Xie is still young, yet was able to hold firm the city—his loyal integrity stands out; We greatly commend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengping an edict to Yiluo said, "Xie is still young, yet he held the city firm—his loyalty stands out, and We greatly commend him.

sentences.zh: 可遣歇詣闕。

translations.literal: Let Xie be sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: Send Xie to court."

sentences.zh: 」伊洛令歇將弟波利等十餘人赴都。

translations.literal: " Yiluo ordered Xie to lead his younger brother Poli and over ten others to go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo sent Xie, with his younger brother Poli and more than ten others, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 正平二年，伊洛朝京師，賜以妻妾、奴婢、田宅、牛羊，拜上將軍，王如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengping, Yiluo came to court at the capital; he was granted wives, concubines, servants, fields, houses, cattle, and sheep; appointed Great General; his kingship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengping Yiluo came to court and was granted wives, concubines, servants, fields, houses, cattle, and sheep; he was made Great General and kept his royal title.

sentences.zh: 興安二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮西大將軍、秦州刺史，諡曰康王。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Qin Province; posthumous name Prince Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Qin Province, with the posthumous name Prince Kang.

sentences.zh: 賜綿絹雜綵五百匹，衣二十七襲。

translations.literal: Granted five hundred bolts of cotton, silk, and mixed brocade, and twenty-seven suits of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted five hundred bolts of cotton, silk, and mixed brocade, and twenty-seven suits of clothing.

sentences.zh: 葬禮依盧魯元故事。

translations.literal: Funeral rites followed the precedent of Lu Luyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral followed the precedent set for Lu Luyuan.

sentences.zh: 歇襲爵。

translations.literal: Xie inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Xie inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 皇興末，拜使持節、平西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Huangxing he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Huangxing era he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 延興三年卒，子伯主襲爵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanxing he died; his son Bozhu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Yanxing; his son Bozhu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 波利，天安二年拜立節將軍，樂官侯。

translations.literal: Poli, in the second year of Tian'an, was appointed General Who Establishes Integrity and Marquis of Yueguan.
translations.idiomatic: Poli, in the second year of Tian'an, was made General Who Establishes Integrity and Marquis of Yueguan.

sentences.zh: 皇興三年卒，兄子洛都襲爵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangxing he died; his elder brother's son Luodu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Huangxing; his elder brother's son Luodu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 宿石，朔方人也，赫連屈孑弟文陳之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Su Shi was a man of Shuofang, the great-grandson of Wen Chen, younger brother of Helian Qujie.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi came from Shuofang; he was the great-grandson of Wen Chen, younger brother of Helian Qujie.

sentences.zh: 天興二年，文陳父子歸闕，太祖嘉之，以宗女妻焉，賜奴婢數十口，拜為上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxing, Wen Chen and his son came to court; Emperor Taizu commended them, gave an imperial clan daughter in marriage, granted several dozen servants, and appointed [him] Great General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxing Wen Chen and his son came to court; Emperor Taizu commended them, gave Wen Chen an imperial clan daughter in marriage, granted him several dozen servants, and made him Great General.

sentences.zh: 祖若豆根，太宗時賜姓宿氏，襲上將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ruodougen, in Emperor Taizong's time, was granted the surname Su; he inherited [the rank of] Great General.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ruodougen was granted the surname Su under Emperor Taizong and inherited the rank of Great General.

sentences.zh: 父沓干，世祖時虎賁幢將。

translations.literal: His father Tagan, in Emperor Shizu's time, was Chief of the Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tagan served under Emperor Shizu as Chief of the Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 從征平涼有功，拜虎威將軍、侍御郎，賜爵漢安男。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Pingliang he had merit; appointed General of Tiger Might and Attendant Secretary; granted the title Viscount of Han'an.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Pingliang and for his service was made General of Tiger Might and Attendant Secretary, enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an.

sentences.zh: 轉中散，遷給事，兼領工曹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Scribe, promoted to Gentleman of Service, and concurrently headed the Works Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Scribe, promoted to Gentleman of Service, and put in charge of the Works Office as well.

sentences.zh: 從駕討和龍，以功賜奴婢十七戶。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage in the campaign against Helong; for merit he was granted seventeen households of servants.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the campaign against Helong and for his service was granted seventeen households of servants.

sentences.zh: 真君四年，從駕討蠕蠕，戰沒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenjun he followed the imperial carriage on a campaign against the Rouran and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenjun he accompanied the emperor against the Rouran and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 世祖悼惜之，詔求沓干子。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu mourned and regretted this and ordered that Tadgan's son be sought out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu mourned his loss and issued an order to find Tadgan's son.

sentences.zh: 時石年甫十一，引見，以幼聽歸。

translations.literal: At the time Shi was only eleven; he was summoned for audience and, because he was young, was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was then only eleven. He was brought before the throne, but because he was still a child he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 年十三，襲爵，擢為中散。

translations.literal: At thirteen he inherited the title and was promoted to Central Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he succeeded to his father's rank and was made Central Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從駕至江，拜宣威將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage to the Yangtze and was appointed General Who Proclaims Might.
translations.idiomatic: When the court marched to the Yangtze he was made General Who Proclaims Might.

sentences.zh: 興光中，遷侍御史，拜中壘將軍，進爵蔡陽子，典宜官曹。

translations.literal: During Xingguang he was transferred to Attendant Censor, appointed General of the Central Rampart, advanced to Marquis of Caiyang, and put in charge of the Bureau of Appropriate Officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xingguang era he became Attendant Censor and General of the Central Rampart, was raised to Marquis of Caiyang, and took charge of the Bureau of Appropriate Officials.

sentences.zh: 遷內行令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Inner Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of Inner Conduct.

sentences.zh: 從幸苑內，遊獵，石於高宗前走馬，道峻，馬倒殞絕，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a hunt in the park, Shi galloped his horse before Emperor Gaozong; the path was steep, the horse fell, and he collapsed as if dead, only reviving after a long while.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunting excursion in the imperial park, Shi galloped ahead of Emperor Gaozong along a steep track. His horse went down and he lay as if dead, not coming to for a long time.

sentences.zh: 由是御馬得制。

translations.literal: From this the imperial horses came under regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After that the emperor's horses were brought under strict control.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘉之，賜綿一百斤，帛五十匹，駿馬一匹，改爵義陽子。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong commended him, granting one hundred jin of cotton, fifty bolts of silk, one fine horse, and changing his title to Marquis of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong praised him and rewarded him with a hundred jin of cotton, fifty bolts of silk, and a fine horse, raising his title to Marquis of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 嘗從獵，高宗親欲射虎。

translations.literal: Once on a hunt Emperor Gaozong himself wished to shoot a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: On one hunt Emperor Gaozong meant to shoot a tiger himself.

sentences.zh: 石叩馬而諫，引高宗至高原上。

translations.literal: Shi reined in his horse and remonstrated, leading Emperor Gaozong up onto high ground.
translations.idiomatic: Shi checked his horse and remonstrated, then led Emperor Gaozong up to higher ground.

sentences.zh: 後虎騰躍殺人。

translations.literal: Later the tiger leaped forth and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the tiger sprang out and killed several men.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「石為忠臣，鞚馬切諫，免虎之害。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Shi is a loyal minister; by reining in his horse and remonstrating earnestly he averted the harm of the tiger.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Shi has proved himself a loyal minister. By reining in his horse and remonstrating with all urgency he spared us the tiger's attack.

sentences.zh: 後有犯罪，宥而勿坐。

translations.literal: If hereafter he commits an offense, pardon him and do not punish.
translations.idiomatic: Should he ever commit an offense hereafter, let him be pardoned and not punished.

sentences.zh: 」賜駿馬一匹。

translations.literal: " He was granted one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: " He was also given a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 尚上谷公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Princess Shanggu and was appointed Commandant of Escort.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Shanggu and was made Commandant of Escort.

sentences.zh: 天安初，遷散騎常侍、吏部尚書，進爵太山公，為北中道都大將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an he was transferred to Regular Palace Attendant and Minister of Personnel, advanced to Duke of Taishan, and made Grand General of the Northern Middle Route.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tian'an era he became Regular Palace Attendant and Minister of Personnel, was raised to Duke of Taishan, and appointed Grand General of the Northern Middle Route.

sentences.zh: [7]延興元年卒。

translations.literal: [7] He died in the first year of Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: [7] He died in the first year of Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 追贈太原王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Prince of Taiyuan, with posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 葬禮依盧魯元故事。

translations.literal: The funeral rites followed the precedent set for Lu Luyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral followed the precedent established for Lu Luyuan.

sentences.zh: 太和初，子倪襲爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe his son Ni inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era his son Ni succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 比部侍御。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor of the Bureau of Comparison.
translations.idiomatic: He became Attendant Censor of the Bureau of Comparison.

sentences.zh: 來大千，[8]代人也。

translations.literal: Lai Daqian [8] was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Daqian [8] came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父初真，從太祖避難叱候山，參創業之功，官至後將軍，武原侯，與在八議。

translations.literal: His father Chuzhen, when he followed Emperor Taizu in taking refuge at Chihou Mountain, took part in the work of founding the dynasty; he reached the rank of Later General and Marquis of Wuyuan and was among the Eight Deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuzhen had followed Emperor Taizu to refuge at Chihou Mountain and shared in the founding of the dynasty, rising to Later General and Marquis of Wuyuan and earning a place among the Eight Deliberations.

sentences.zh: 大千驍果，善騎射，為騎都尉。

translations.literal: Daqian was fierce and resolute, skilled at mounted archery, and became Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Daqian was bold and formidable, a master of mounted archery, and was made Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永興初，襲爵，遷中散。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxing he inherited the title and was transferred to Central Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongxing era he succeeded to his father's rank and was made Central Attendant.

sentences.zh: 至於朝賀之日，大千常著御鎧，盤馬殿前，朝臣莫不嗟歎。

translations.literal: On days of court felicitation Daqian often wore imperial armor and wheeled his horse before the hall; the court ministers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: On court festival days Daqian would appear in imperial armor and wheel his horse before the hall, to the wonder of every minister present.

sentences.zh: 遷內幢將，典宿衞禁旅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inner Banner General and put in charge of the palace guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Inner Banner General and placed in command of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 大千用法嚴明，上下齊肅。

translations.literal: Daqian applied the law with strict clarity, and superiors and subordinates alike were orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Daqian enforced the law with stern clarity, and discipline ran from top to bottom.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太宗校獵，見虎在高巖上，大千持矟直前刺之，應手而死。

translations.literal: Once, following Emperor Taizong on a hunting drill, he saw a tiger on a high cliff; Daqian took his spear and thrust straight forward, and it died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while hunting with Emperor Taizong, he spotted a tiger on a high cliff. Daqian drove his spear home at a single thrust and killed it on the spot.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其勇壯，又為殿中給事。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong praised his courage and strength and also made him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong admired his courage and also appointed him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐祚，與襄城公盧魯元等七人俱為常侍，持仗侍衞，晝夜不離左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he and Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and six others all became Regular Attendants, holding staffs as guards and never leaving his side day or night.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu came to the throne, Daqian and Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and six others were all made Regular Attendants, armed with ceremonial staffs and attending him day and night without leave.

sentences.zh: 從討赫連昌，共長孫道生與賊交戰。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helian Chang and, together with Changsun Daosheng, joined battle with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Helian Chang and, together with Changsun Daosheng, fought the enemy in the field.

sentences.zh: 道生馬倒，為賊所擊，大千馳救，賊眾散走。

translations.literal: Daosheng's horse fell and he was struck by the enemy; Daqian raced to the rescue and the enemy force scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng's horse went down under enemy blows; Daqian galloped to his aid and the foe broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 大千扶道生上馬，遂得免。

translations.literal: Daqian helped Daosheng mount his horse, and thus he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Daqian helped Daosheng back into the saddle and saw him safely away.

sentences.zh: 從討蠕蠕，戰功居多。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Rouran, and most of the battle merit was his.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against the Rouran he accounted for the greater part of the victory.

sentences.zh: 遷征北大將軍，賜爵廬陵公，鎮雲中，兼統白道軍事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Great General Who Conquers the North, granted the title Duke of Luling, stationed at Yunzhong, and additionally commanded White Road military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Great General Who Conquers the North and Duke of Luling, posted to Yunzhong with overall command of White Road military affairs.

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text missing in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 賊北叛，大千前後追擊，莫不平殄。

translations.literal: When the rebels fled north, Daqian pursued them again and again and utterly destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fled north, Daqian pursued them in successive actions until none were left.

sentences.zh: 延和初，車駕北伐，大千為前鋒，大破虜軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanhe the imperial carriage made a northern campaign; Daqian served as vanguard and greatly defeated the barbarian army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanhe era, on the northern expedition, Daqian led the vanguard and routed the enemy army.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其壯勇，數有戰功，兼悉北境險要，詔大千巡撫六鎮，以防寇虜。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, because of his courage and strength, his repeated battle achievements, and his thorough knowledge of the northern frontier's strategic points, ordered Daqian to inspect and pacify the six garrisons to guard against invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, knowing Daqian's valor, his record of victories, and his mastery of the northern frontier, ordered him to tour and secure the six garrisons against invasion.

sentences.zh: 經略布置，甚得事宜。

translations.literal: His planning and deployment were very appropriate to the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: His arrangements were admirably suited to the situation.

sentences.zh: 後吐京胡反，以大千為都將討平之。

translations.literal: Later, when the Tujing Hu rebelled, Daqian was made commander-in-chief and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tujing Hu rose in rebellion afterward, Daqian was appointed commander-in-chief and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 在吐京卒，喪還，停於平城南。

translations.literal: He died at Tujing; when the coffin was returned it halted south of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Tujing, and on the return of his coffin it was halted south of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖出，還，見而問之，左右以對，世祖悼歎者良久。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu went out and, on returning, saw it and asked about it; his attendants answered, and Emperor Shizu mourned and sighed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu went out and, on his return, saw the coffin and asked what it was. When his attendants told him, he mourned and sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「大千忠勇盡節，功在可嘉，今聽喪入殯城內。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Daqian was loyal and brave to the utmost in devotion; his merit deserves commendation. He is now permitted to have his coffin brought inside the city for burial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran, "Daqian served with absolute loyalty and courage; his merit is beyond praise. Let his coffin be brought within the city for burial.

sentences.zh: 」贈司空，諡曰莊公。

translations.literal: " He was posthumously awarded Minister of Works, with posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: " He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子丘頹，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Qiutui inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiutui succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 降為晉興侯。

translations.literal: The title was reduced to Marquis of Jinxing.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was lowered to Marquis of Jinxing.

sentences.zh: 拜安遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 從駕到江，進右將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage to the Yangtze and was promoted to Right General.
translations.idiomatic: When the court marched to the Yangtze he was promoted to Right General.

sentences.zh: 和平中，遷中散，轉相曹都典奉事。

translations.literal: During Heping he was transferred to Central Attendant and then made Chief of Tribute Affairs in the Ministry of Works Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heping era he became Central Attendant and then Chief of Tribute Affairs in the Ministry of Works Bureau.

sentences.zh: 皇興四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Huangxing.

sentences.zh: 贈寧南將軍、陳留公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Chenliu, with posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Chenliu, with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 子蕇襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 丘頹弟提，官至監御曹給事，冠軍將軍，兗州刺史，濮陽侯。

translations.literal: Qiutui's younger brother Ti reached the posts of Supervisor of the Imperial Guard Bureau Attendant, Champion General, Inspector of Yan Province, and Marquis of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiutui's younger brother Ti rose to Supervisor of the Imperial Guard Bureau Attendant, Champion General, Inspector of Yan Province, and Marquis of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 太和十年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 周幾，代人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Ji was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父千，有功太祖之世，賜爵順陽侯。

translations.literal: His father Qian had merit in Emperor Taizu's time and was granted the title Marquis of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian won distinction under Emperor Taizu and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 坐事死。

translations.literal: He was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was put to death for a crime.

sentences.zh: 幾少以善騎射為獵郎。

translations.literal: Ji in his youth, because he was skilled at mounted archery, became a Hunter Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ji was so skilled at mounted archery that he was made a Hunter Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，[9]為殿中侍御史，掌宿衞禁兵，斷決稱職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne [9] he became Attendant Censor within the Palace, in charge of the palace guard troops; his judgments fit his office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne [9] he was made Attendant Censor within the Palace and put in charge of the palace guard; his decisions were always sound.

sentences.zh: 遷左民尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Left People.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Left People.

sentences.zh: 神瑞中，并州飢民遊食山東，詔幾領眾鎮博陵之魯口以安集之。

translations.literal: During Shenrui, famine refugees from Bing Province wandered east of the mountains; an edict ordered Ji to lead troops to garrison the Luo mouth at Boling and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenrui era, starving refugees from Bing Province drifted east of the mountains, and Ji was ordered to lead troops to the Luo mouth at Boling to receive and settle them.

sentences.zh: 泰常初，白澗、行唐民數千家負嶮不供輸稅，幾與安康子長孫道生宣示禍福，逃民遂還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, several thousand households of Baijian and Xingtang held the defiles and refused to pay tribute; Ji, together with Ankangzi Changsun Daosheng, proclaimed fortune and misfortune to them, and the fugitive people then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era several thousand households in Baijian and Xingtang held the mountain passes and refused tribute. Ji and Ankangzi Changsun Daosheng set out the consequences before them, and the fugitives came back.

sentences.zh: 于時郡縣斬叛胡翟猛雀於林慮山，猛雀遺種竄於行唐及襄國。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures and counties executed the rebel Hu Zhai Mengque at Linyu Mountain; Mengque's surviving followers hid themselves in Xingtang and Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: About that time the prefectures and counties executed the rebel Hu chieftain Mengque at Linyu Mountain, but Mengque's remaining followers hid out in Xingtang and Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 幾追討，盡誅之。

translations.literal: Ji pursued and attacked them and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji hunted them down and put every one of them to death.

sentences.zh: 後為寧朔將軍，拒司馬德宗將劉裕於南，破毛德祖於土樓。

translations.literal: Later he became General Who Pacifies the North, resisted Liu Yu, a general of Sima Dezong, in the south, and defeated Mao Dezu at Tulou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the North, held Liu Yu, a general of Sima Dezong, in the south, and broke Mao Dezu at Tulou.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵交阯侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title Marquis of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 世祖以幾有智勇，遣鎮河南，威信著于外境。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, because Ji had wisdom and courage, sent him to garrison Henan; his prestige and trust were noted in the outer borders.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, recognizing Ji's wisdom and courage, posted him to garrison Henan, where his authority was felt far beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 幾常嫌奚斤等綏撫關中失和，百姓不附。

translations.literal: Ji often resented that Xi Jin and the others, in pacifying Guanzhong, had lost harmony and the common people were not attached.
translations.idiomatic: Ji often blamed Xi Jin and his colleagues for mishandling the pacification of Guanzhong so badly that the people would not rally to the court.

sentences.zh: 每至言論，形於聲色。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of it, it showed in his voice and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the subject came up, his anger showed plainly in face and voice.

sentences.zh: 斤等憚焉。

translations.literal: Jin and the others feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin and the rest were afraid of him.

sentences.zh: 進號宋兵將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General of Song Troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Song Troops.

sentences.zh: 率洛州刺史于栗磾以萬人襲陝城，卒于軍，軍人無不歎惜之。

translations.literal: He led Inspector of Luo Province Yu Libian with ten thousand men in a surprise attack on Shancheng and died in the army; the soldiers all sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Leading Inspector of Luo Province Yu Libian and ten thousand men in a raid on Shancheng, he died in camp, and every soldier mourned him.

sentences.zh: 歸葬京師。

translations.literal: He was returned for burial in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His body was brought back to the capital for burial.

sentences.zh: 追贈交阯公，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded Duke of Jiaozhi, with posthumous name Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jiaozhi, with the posthumous name Huan.

sentences.zh: 子步，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Bu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子安國，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Anguo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anguo succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 太和中，討蠕蠕，失利，伏法。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, on a campaign against the Rouran, he suffered defeat and was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he took the field against the Rouran, met defeat, and was put to death by sentence of law.

sentences.zh: 爵除。

translations.literal: The title was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 豆代田，代人也。

translations.literal: Dou Daitian was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Daitian came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 太宗時以善騎射為內細射。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's time, because he was skilled at mounted archery, he became Inner Fine Archer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong his skill at mounted archery won him appointment as Inner Fine Archer.

sentences.zh: 從攻虎牢，詔代田登樓射賊，矢不虛發。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Hulao; an edict ordered Daitian to ascend the tower and shoot at the enemy, and his arrows never missed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Hulao, was ordered up onto the tower to shoot at the enemy, and never wasted an arrow.

sentences.zh: 與奚斤前鋒先入，擒劉義隆將毛德祖并長史、司馬三人。

translations.literal: With Xi Jin in the vanguard he entered first and captured Liu Yilong's general Mao Dezu together with the chief clerk and marshal—three men in all.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in Xi Jin's vanguard he went in first and took Liu Yilong's general Mao Dezu along with the chief clerk and marshal—three captives in all.

sentences.zh: 以功遷內三郎。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Inner Third Lang.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made Inner Third Lang.

sentences.zh: 從討赫連昌，乘勝追賊，入其宮門，門閉，代田踰宮而出。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helian Chang, pursued the enemy in victory, entered their palace gate; the gate closed, and Daitian scaled the palace wall and got out.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Helian Chang he pressed the pursuit into the palace itself. When the gate slammed shut behind him, he climbed the palace wall and escaped.

sentences.zh: 世祖壯之，拜勇武將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu admired this and appointed him Brave and Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was impressed and made him Brave and Martial General.

sentences.zh: 後從駕平昌，以戰功賜奴婢十五口，黃金百斤，銀百斤。

translations.literal: Later he followed the imperial carriage in pacifying Chang; for battle merit he was granted fifteen male and female servants, one hundred jin of gold, and one hundred jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor in the pacification of Chang and, for his battlefield service, was given fifteen bond servants plus a hundred jin of gold and a hundred jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，討蠕蠕，賜爵關中侯。

translations.literal: During Shenjuan he campaigned against the Rouran and was granted the title Marquis of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenjuan era he fought the Rouran and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 從討平涼，擊破赫連定，得奚斤等。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Pingliang, defeated Helian Ding, and captured Xi Jin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Pingliang, broke Helian Ding, and took Xi Jin and his fellows prisoner.

sentences.zh: 世祖以定妻賜之，詔斤膝行授酒於代田。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu gave Ding's wife to him and ordered Jin to crawl on his knees and offer wine to Daitian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu gave Helian Ding's wife to Daitian and ordered Xi Jin to crawl forward on his knees and present him with wine.

sentences.zh: 敕斤曰：「全爾身命者，代田功也。

translations.literal: He charged Jin: "The one who preserved your life and person—it is Daitian's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xi Jin, "The man who saved your life was Daitian.

sentences.zh: 」改爵井陘侯，加散騎常侍、右衞將軍、領內都幢將。

translations.literal: " His title was changed to Marquis of Jingxing; he was additionally made Regular Palace Attendant, Right Guard General, and commander of the Inner Banner General.
translations.idiomatic: " His title was changed to Marquis of Jingxing, and he was further made Regular Palace Attendant, Right Guard General, and commander of the Inner Banner General.

sentences.zh: 從討和龍，戰功居多，遷殿中尚書，賜奴婢六十口。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helong; his battle merit was mostly outstanding, and he was transferred to Director within the Palace and granted sixty male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Helong his achievements stood out above the rest; he was made Director within the Palace and given sixty bond servants.

sentences.zh: 以前後軍功，進爵長廣公，加平東將軍。

translations.literal: For his former and latter military achievements he was advanced to Duke of Changgung and additionally made General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: For his cumulative military service he was raised to Duke of Changgung and made General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 從駕南討。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 轉太子太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 出為統萬鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General of the Tongwan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General of the Tongwan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 興安中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Xing'an era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xing'an reign.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、安東大將軍、長廣王，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Prince of Changguang; posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the East, enfeoffed as Prince of Changguang, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子求周，為內三郎。

translations.literal: His son Qiuzhou was a Third Lang within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiuzhou served as Third Lang within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 從駕到江，賜爵五等子。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial campaign to the Yangtze and was granted the title viscount of the fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor south to the Yangtze and was enfeoffed as a fifth-rank viscount.

sentences.zh: 又進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was later raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 後襲父爵。

translations.literal: Later he inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded to his father's title.

sentences.zh: 為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 皇興二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Huangxing.

sentences.zh: 贈征北大將軍、長廣王，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Conquers the North and Prince of Changguang; posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Conquers the North and Prince of Changguang, with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 子多侯襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Duohou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duohou succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 子豆，初為三郎，遷軍將。

translations.literal: His son Dou, at first a Third Lang, was transferred to General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dou began as a Third Lang and was promoted to General.

sentences.zh: 卒于長樂太守。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Administrator of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Administrator of Changle.

sentences.zh: 閭大肥，蠕蠕人也。

translations.literal: Lü Dafei was a man of the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dafei was a man of the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，與其弟大埿倍頤率宗族歸國。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taizu, he and his younger brother Da Ai Beiyi led their clan to submit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizu's reign he and his younger brother Da Ai Beiyi led their clan into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，尚華陰公主，賜爵其思子，與其弟並為上賓，入八議。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu favored him, gave him Princess Huayin in marriage, granted the title Viscount of Qisi, and with his brother made them both honored guests and admitted them to the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu took a liking to him, married him to Princess Huayin, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Qisi, and with his brother enrolled both among the court's honored guests in the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，進大肥為內都大官，增爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Dafei was promoted to Grand Director of Internal Affairs and his title was raised to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, Dafei was made Grand Director of Internal Affairs and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 神瑞中，為都將，討越勒部於跋那山，大破之。

translations.literal: In the Shenrui era he was a commander-general and campaigned against the Yuele tribe at Bana Mountain, crushing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenrui era he served as commander-general, attacked the Yuele tribe at Bana Mountain, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 泰常初，復為都將，領禁兵討蠕蠕，獲其大將莫孤渾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he again served as commander-general, leading the palace guard to campaign against the Rouran and capturing their general Moguhun.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taichang he again commanded the guard troops against the Rouran and took their general Moguhun prisoner.

sentences.zh: 宜城王奚斤之攻虎牢也，大肥與娥清領十二軍出中道，略地高平、金鄉，東至泰山。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin attacked Hulao, Dafei with E Qing led twelve armies on the middle route, raiding Gaoping and Jinxiang and reaching east to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin besieged Hulao, Dafei and E Qing led twelve armies on the central route, sweeping through Gaoping and Jinxiang as far east as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 假大肥使持節、安陽公，鎮撫陳汝。

translations.literal: Dafei was given acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Duke of Anyang to pacify Chen and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Dafei was made acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Duke of Anyang to pacify Chen and Ru.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，復與奚斤出雲中白道討大檀，破之。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign he again marched with Xi Jin from Bai Road in Yunzhong to campaign against Datan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign he again marched with Xi Jin from Bai Road in Yunzhong against Datan and broke his forces.

sentences.zh: 還為內都大官。

translations.literal: On returning he was Grand Director of Internal Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Grand Director of Internal Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出除使持節、冀青二州刺史，假滎陽公。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Inspector of Ji and Qing provinces, with the acting title Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Ji and Qing with the Staff of Authority and the acting title Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 尋徵還，位特進。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and given the rank of Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and granted the rank of Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 復出為冀青二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again sent out as Inspector of Ji and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was again posted as Inspector of Ji and Qing.

sentences.zh: 尋入為內都大官。

translations.literal: Soon he re-entered court as Grand Director of Internal Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Grand Director of Internal Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從討赫連昌，以功授滎陽公。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helian Chang and for merit was granted the title Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Helian Chang and for his service was enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 公主薨，復尚濩澤公主。

translations.literal: When the princess died he again married Princess Huoze.
translations.idiomatic: After his first princess consort died he was given Princess Huoze in marriage.

sentences.zh: 又為都將，擊大檀，大破之。

translations.literal: He again served as commander-general, struck Datan, and crushed him.
translations.idiomatic: Again as commander-general he attacked Datan and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 還至渴侯山，遂討東部高車於巳尼陂。

translations.literal: Returning to Kehou Mountain, he then campaigned against the eastern Gaoche at Sini Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: On the march back to Kehou Mountain he turned against the eastern Gaoche at Sini Marsh.

sentences.zh: 又征平涼，並有功。

translations.literal: He also campaigned against Pingliang, with merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the campaign against Pingliang, earning merit in both actions.

sentences.zh: 世祖將拜大肥為王，遇疾卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was about to enfeoff Dafei as prince when Dafei fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was on the point of raising Dafei to princely rank when illness carried him off.

sentences.zh: 追贈中山王。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 子賀，早卒。

translations.literal: His son He died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son He died young.

sentences.zh: 大肥弟驎，襲爵。

translations.literal: Dafei's younger brother Lin inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Dafei's younger brother Lin succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 出為仇池鎮將。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General of the Chouci Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General of the Chouci Garrison.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving no son.

sentences.zh: 弟鳳，襲爵。

translations.literal: His younger brother Feng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Feng succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 高宗時為內都大官，出為鎮南將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's time he was Grand Director of Internal Affairs and was sent out as General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he served as Grand Director of Internal Affairs, then was sent out as General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He died without sons; the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He died without an heir and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 尉撥，代人也。

translations.literal: Wei Bo was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 父那，濮陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Na was Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Na was Administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 撥為太學生，募從兗州刺史羅忸擊賊於陳汝，有功，賜爵介休男。

translations.literal: Bo was a student at the Imperial Academy; he volunteered to follow Inspector of Yan Province Luo Ni in attacking bandits in Chen and Ru, had merit, and was granted the title Viscount of Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: Bo studied at the Imperial Academy, volunteered to follow Inspector of Yan Province Luo Ni against bandits in Chen and Ru, distinguished himself, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 從討和龍，遷虎賁帥，轉千人軍將。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Helong, was transferred to commandant of the Tiger Guard, then commander of the Thousand-man Army.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Helong, was made commandant of the Tiger Guard, then commander of a thousand-man detachment.

sentences.zh: 又從樂平王丕討和龍。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince of Le Ping Pi in campaigning against Helong.
translations.idiomatic: He again marched with Prince of Le Ping Pi against Helong.

sentences.zh: 除涼州軍將，擊吐谷渾，獲其人一千餘落。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commander of Liang Province, attacked the Tuyuhun, and captured more than a thousand of their households.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed military commander of Liang Province, he attacked the Tuyuhun and took more than a thousand households captive.

sentences.zh: 後吐谷渾小將率三百餘落來降，尋復亡叛，撥率騎追之，盡獲而還。

translations.literal: Later a Tuyuhun junior commander led more than three hundred households to surrender, then soon rebelled and fled; Bo led cavalry in pursuit, captured them all, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Tuyuhun subordinate brought three hundred-odd households in surrender, then rebelled and fled; Bo pursued with cavalry, recaptured every one of them, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為子。

translations.literal: For merit his title was advanced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: For his service his rank was raised to viscount.

sentences.zh: [10]遷晉昌鎮將，綏懷邊民，甚著稱績。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Jinchang Garrison, soothed the frontier people, and won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to the Jinchang garrison, he won over the frontier populace and earned wide praise.

sentences.zh: 入為知臣監。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as Director of the Office of Knowing Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Director of the Office of Knowing Ministers.

sentences.zh: 出為杏城鎮將，在任九年，大收民和，山民一千餘家、上郡徒各、盧水胡八百餘落，盡附為民。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General of the Xingcheng Garrison; in nine years in office he greatly won the people's hearts, and more than a thousand mountain households of Shang commandery, the Tuge, and eight hundred-odd households of the Lushui Hu all submitted and became registered subjects.
translations.idiomatic: As General of the Xingcheng Garrison he served nine years and won the people's trust; more than a thousand mountain households in Shang commandery, the Tuge, and eight hundred-odd Lushui Hu households all submitted and were registered as subjects.

sentences.zh: 高宗以撥清平有惠績，賜以衣服。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, because Bo was upright and had benevolent achievements, bestowed clothing on him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong rewarded him with robes for his integrity and his record of benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，為北征都將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu took the throne, [Bo] was Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu came to the throne, Bo was made Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 復為都將，南攻懸瓠，破劉彧將朱湛之水軍三千人，拜懸瓠鎮將，加員外散騎常侍，進爵安城侯。

translations.literal: He again served as commander-general, attacked Xuanchi in the south, defeated three thousand men of Liu Yu's general Zhu Zhanzhi on the water, was appointed General of the Xuanchi Garrison, given the additional title Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and advanced to Marquis of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Again commanding troops he struck south at Xuanchi, destroyed three thousand of Liu Yu's men under Zhu Zhanzhi on the river, was made General of the Xuanchi Garrison and Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and raised to Marquis of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘉其聲效，復賜衣服。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu praised his renown and effectiveness and again bestowed clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu praised his reputation and results and again granted him robes.

sentences.zh: 轉平南將軍、北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Northern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Northern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後洛州民田智度聚黨謀逆。

translations.literal: Later the people of Luozhou, Tian Zhidu, gathered a faction and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tian Zhidu of Luozhou gathered followers and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔撥乘傳發豫州兵與洛州刺史丘頓擊之，獲智度，送京師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bo to travel post-haste and mobilize Yuzhou troops with Inspector of Luozhou Qiu Dun to attack them; Zhidu was captured and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Bo post-haste to raise Yuzhou troops and, with Inspector of Luozhou Qiu Dun, crush the plot; Zhidu was taken and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 撥卒，贈冠軍將軍，諡敬侯。

translations.literal: Bo died; posthumously awarded General of Champion Cavalry; posthumous name Jinghou.
translations.idiomatic: Bo died and was posthumously made General of Champion Cavalry, with the posthumous name Jinghou.

sentences.zh: 陸真，代人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhen was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhen was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 父洛侯，秦州長史。

translations.literal: His father Luohou was Chief Clerk of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luohou was Chief Clerk of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 真少善騎射。

translations.literal: Zhen from youth was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhen was skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，以真膂力過人，拜內三郎。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign, because Zhen's physical strength surpassed others, he was appointed Third Lang within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign his exceptional strength won him appointment as Third Lang within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，所在摧鋒陷陳，前後以功屢受賞賜。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns; wherever he went he broke the enemy vanguard and pierced their formations; before and after he repeatedly received rewards for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in campaign after campaign, always at the point of the assault, and was rewarded again and again.

sentences.zh: 真君中，從討蠕蠕，以功賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era he followed the campaign against the Rouran and for merit was granted the title Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenjun era he campaigned against the Rouran and was enfeoffed as Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 後攻懸瓠，登樓臨射城中，弦不虛發。

translations.literal: Later he attacked Xuanchi, mounted the tower and shot down into the city; not an arrow missed.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Xuanchi he climbed a tower and shot into the city; every arrow found its mark.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆將王玄謨眾數萬人寇滑臺，真從世祖討之。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong's general Wang Xuanymo with tens of thousands of men invaded Huatai; Zhen followed Emperor Shizu to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanymo of Liu Yilong marched on Huatai with tens of thousands of men; Zhen followed Emperor Shizu against him.

sentences.zh: 夜與數人乘小船突玄謨軍，入城撫慰，登城，巡行賊營中，乃還渡河。

translations.literal: At night with several men he took a small boat and burst into Xuanymo's army, entered the city to reassure the garrison, mounted the wall, and patrolled through the enemy camps before crossing the river back.
