translations.idiomatic: By night he took a small boat with a handful of men, slipped through Xuanymo's lines, entered the city to hearten the defenders, walked the walls, threaded the enemy camps, and crossed back over the river.

sentences.zh: 至明，玄謨敗走。

translations.literal: At dawn Xuanymo was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Xuanymo's army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 從駕至江，真再破賊軍，拜建武將軍、石城子。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial campaign to the Yangtze; Zhen again defeated the enemy army and was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Viscount of Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign to the Yangtze he again routed the enemy and was made General Who Establishes Might and Viscount of Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 還攻盱眙，真功居多，遷給事中，典太倉事。

translations.literal: On returning he attacked Xuyi; Zhen's merit was greatest; he was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and put in charge of the Grand Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he helped take Xuyi, where his contribution stood foremost; he was made Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and superintendent of the Grand Granary.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，拜冠軍將軍，進爵都昌侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne he was appointed General of Champion Cavalry and advanced to Marquis of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne he was made General of Champion Cavalry and raised to Marquis of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，選部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時丁零數千家寇竊并定，真與并州刺史乞伏成龍自樂平東入，與定州刺史許崇之併力討滅。

translations.literal: At that time several thousand households of the Dingling raided and plundered Bing and Ding; Zhen with Inspector of Bing Province Qifu Chenglong entered from the east at Leping and with Inspector of Ding Province Xu Chongzhi combined forces to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand Dingling households turned to raiding in Bing and Ding, Zhen marched from Leping in the east with Inspector of Bing Province Qifu Chenglong and, joining Inspector of Ding Province Xu Chongzhi, wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 從駕巡東海，以真為寧西將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial tour of the Eastern Sea; Zhen was made General Who Stills the West.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial tour of the Eastern Sea he was made General Who Stills the West.

sentences.zh: 尋遷安西將軍、長安鎮將，假建平公。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the West and General of the Chang'an Garrison, with the acting title Duke of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West and General of the Chang'an Garrison, with the acting title Duke of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 胡賊帥賀略孫聚眾千餘人叛于石樓。

translations.literal: The Hu bandit chief He Luesun gathered more than a thousand men and rebelled at Shilou.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu chieftain He Luesun gathered a thousand followers and rebelled at Shilou.

sentences.zh: 真擊破之，殺五百餘人。

translations.literal: Zhen defeated them and killed more than five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen routed them and killed more than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 是時，初置長蛇鎮，真率眾築城，未訖，而氐豪仇傉檀等反叛，氐民咸應，其眾甚盛。

translations.literal: At that time the Changshe Garrison was first established; Zhen led the multitude to build the fort, but before it was finished the Di chieftain Qiu Nutan and others rebelled and the Di people all rose; their numbers were very great.
translations.idiomatic: When the new Changshe garrison was still rising from the ground, the Di chieftain Qiu Nutan rebelled and the Di clans answered in force.

sentences.zh: 真擊平之，殺四千餘人，卒城長蛇而還。

translations.literal: Zhen attacked and pacified them, killed more than four thousand men, finished the fort at Changshe, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen crushed the revolt, killed more than four thousand, completed the Changshe fort, and returned.

sentences.zh: 東平王道符反于長安，殺雍州刺史魚玄明，關中草草。

translations.literal: Prince of Dongping Daofu rebelled at Chang'an, killed Inspector of Yong Province Yu Xuanming, and the Guanzhong region was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Dongping Daofu rose at Chang'an, murdered Inspector of Yong Province Yu Xuanming, and all Guanzhong was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 以真為長安鎮將，賜爵河南公。

translations.literal: Zhen was made General of the Chang'an Garrison and granted the title Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was posted as General of the Chang'an Garrison and enfeoffed as Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 長安兵民，素伏威信，真到，撫慰之，皆怡然安靜。

translations.literal: The soldiers and people of Chang'an had long submitted to his authority and reputation; when Zhen arrived he reassured them and all were calmly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chang'an had long known his authority; when he arrived they took heart and the city settled.

sentences.zh: 咸陽民趙昌受劉彧署龍驤將軍，扇動鄠、𥂕厔二縣，聚黨數百人據赤谷以叛。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang of Xianyang, commissioned by Liu Yu as General of Flying Cavalry, incited E and Zhouzhi counties; he gathered several hundred followers and held Chigu Valley in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang of Xianyang, whom Liu Yu had made General of Flying Cavalry, stirred up E and Zhouzhi; several hundred men rallied to him and seized Chigu Valley.

sentences.zh: 真與雍州刺史劉邈討平之，昌單騎走免。

translations.literal: Zhen with Inspector of Yong Province Liu Miao campaigned and pacified them; Chang fled alone on horseback and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Inspector of Yong Province Liu Miao put down the revolt; Chang alone escaped on horseback.

sentences.zh: 後鄠縣民王稚兄弟，聚二千餘人，招引趙昌。

translations.literal: Later the brothers Wang Zhi of E County gathered more than two thousand men and summoned Zhao Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Later the brothers Wang Zhi of E County mustered more than two thousand men and called Zhao Chang to join them.

sentences.zh: 始平、石安、池陽、靈武四縣人皆應之，眾至五千，據治谷堡。

translations.literal: The people of Shiping, Shi'an, Chiyang, and Lingwu all responded; the host reached five thousand and held Zhigu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: People from Shiping, Shi'an, Chiyang, and Lingwu rose with them until five thousand held Zhigu Fort.

sentences.zh: 時詔南郡王李惠等領步騎六千討昌。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered Prince of Nanjun Li Hui and others to lead six thousand foot and horse to campaign against Chang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then sent Prince of Nanjun Li Hui with six thousand foot and horse against Chang.

sentences.zh: 真以大軍未至，慮昌滋蔓，與雍州刺史劉邈討昌。

translations.literal: Zhen, fearing that before the main army arrived Chang would spread further, with Inspector of Yong Province Liu Miao campaigned against Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Chang would spread before the main force arrived, Zhen and Inspector of Yong Province Liu Miao moved against him at once.

sentences.zh: 昌出營拒戰，真擊破之，斬昌及賊首三千餘級，傳首京師，并誅其黨與七百餘人，獲男女一千餘口。

translations.literal: Chang came out of camp to resist; Zhen defeated him, beheaded Chang and more than three thousand bandit chiefs, sent the heads to the capital, and also executed more than seven hundred accomplices, capturing more than a thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Chang marched out to give battle; Zhen broke him, beheaded Chang and three thousand-odd ringleaders, sent the heads to the capital, executed seven hundred more of his followers, and took more than a thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 雍州民夷，莫不震伏。

translations.literal: The common people and tribes of Yong Province were all awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Every household and tribe in Yong Province bowed to his authority.

sentences.zh: 在鎮數年，甚著威稱。

translations.literal: He was at the garrison several years and won great renown for his authority.
translations.idiomatic: He held the garrison several years and his stern reputation spread far.

sentences.zh: 延興二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yansing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yansing.

sentences.zh: 歸葬京師，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He was buried in the capital; posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: His body was returned to the capital for burial; his posthumous name was Lie.

sentences.zh: 子延，字契胡提，頗有氣幹，襲爵河南公。

translations.literal: His son Yan, style Qihuti, had considerable force of character; he inherited the title Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, styled Qihuti, was a man of force and spirit and succeeded as Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 累遷歷長安鎮將，拜安南將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted and served as General of the Chang'an Garrison; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to General of the Chang'an Garrison, then General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 例降，改封汝陽侯。

translations.literal: By precedent [his title] was reduced; he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent his rank was reduced and he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 京兆王愉為徐州刺史，以延為愉府司馬，帶彭城內史。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yu was Inspector of Xuzhou; Yan was made staff officer in Yu's headquarters with the concurrent post of Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu was Inspector of Xuzhou, Yan served as his staff officer and concurrently as Administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除武川鎮將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was appointed General of the Wuchuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhengshi he was made General of the Wuchuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 入除太僕卿。

translations.literal: He entered [court] as appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 都督沃野、武川、懷朔三鎮諸軍事、安北將軍、懷朔鎮大將，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for the Woye, Wuchuan, and Huaishuo garrisons, General Who Pacifies the North, and General of the Huaishuo Garrison, with the additional title Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in command of the Woye, Wuchuan, and Huaishuo garrisons as General Who Pacifies the North and General of Huaishuo, with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 正光初，拜金紫光祿大夫，復除太僕卿。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhengguang era he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and again appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhengguang he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon and again appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 受使綏慰秀容，為牧子所害。

translations.literal: Commissioned to soothe Xiurong, he was killed by herdsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to pacify Xiurong, he was murdered by local herdsmen.

sentences.zh: 弟什夤，太府卿、平東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shiyin was Minister of the Imperial Treasury, General Who Pacifies the East, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shiyin served as Minister of the Imperial Treasury, General Who Pacifies the East, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 建義初，拜都官尚書。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyi he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyi he was made Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒於平南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died while serving as General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 呂洛拔，代人也。

translations.literal: Lü Luoba was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Luoba was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖渴侯，昭成時率戶五千歸國。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kehou, in the time of Emperor Zhaocheng, led five thousand households to submit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kehou, in Emperor Zhaocheng's reign, led five thousand households into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 祖肥，濮陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fei was Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fei was Administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 父匹知，世祖時為西部長、滎陽公。

translations.literal: His father Pizhi, in Emperor Shizu's time, was Chief of the Western Department and Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pizhi, under Emperor Shizu, was Chief of the Western Department and Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 洛拔以壯勇知名，高宗末為平原鎮都將。

translations.literal: Luoba was known for strength and courage; at the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was commander-general of the Pingyuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Luoba was famed for strength and valor; in the late Gaozong years he commanded the Pingyuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 劉彧徐州刺史薛安都歸誠，請援。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Xuzhou, Xue Andu, submitted in good faith and asked for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu, Liu Yu's Inspector of Xuzhou, pledged allegiance and begged for relief.

sentences.zh: 詔遣尉元率眾救之，洛拔隨元入彭城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wei Yuan to lead troops to rescue him; Luoba followed Yuan into Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Wei Yuan with an army to his aid; Luoba marched in with Yuan to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 彧將張永遣將王茂之領兵五千向武原，援其運車。

translations.literal: Yu's general Zhang Yong sent the commander Wang Maozhi with five thousand men toward Wuyuan to relieve the supply convoy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's general Zhang Yong dispatched Wang Maozhi with five thousand men toward Wuyuan to cover the supply train.

sentences.zh: 元遣洛拔率騎詣武原擊之。

translations.literal: Yuan sent Luoba with cavalry to Wuyuan to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent Luoba with cavalry to strike them at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 格戰二日，手殺九人。

translations.literal: They fought hand to hand for two days; he personally killed nine men.
translations.idiomatic: For two days they fought at close quarters; Luoba himself killed nine men.

sentences.zh: 奪賊運車二百餘乘，牛二百五十頭。

translations.literal: They seized more than two hundred enemy supply carts and two hundred fifty oxen.
translations.idiomatic: They captured more than two hundred supply wagons and two hundred fifty oxen.

sentences.zh: 仍共擊張永，大敗之。

translations.literal: They then jointly attacked Zhang Yong and crushed him.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned on Zhang Yong together and routed him.

sentences.zh: 賜爵成武侯，加建義將軍。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Chengwu and additionally named General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengwu and made General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 年五十六，卒。

translations.literal: At age fifty-six he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 長子文祖，顯祖以其勳臣子，補龍牧曹奏事中散。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wenzu—in Emperor Xianzu's time, because he was the son of a meritorious minister—was appointed Attendant Drafting Clerk in the Dragon Pasturage Office.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wenzu, as the son of a meritorious minister, was given a post as Attendant Drafting Clerk in the Dragon Pasturage Office under Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 以牧產不滋，坐徙於武川鎮。

translations.literal: Because pasturage did not increase, he was sentenced to exile at the Wuchuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the herds failed to multiply he was banished to the Wuchuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 後文祖以舊語譯注皇誥，辭義通辯，超授陽平太守。

translations.literal: Later Wenzu translated and annotated the imperial proclamations in the old language; his wording was lucid and eloquent, and he was exceptionally appointed Administrator of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenzu translated and glossed the imperial proclamations in the old tongue with clear, forceful prose and was abruptly appointed Administrator of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 未拜，轉為外都曹奏事中散。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment he was transferred to Attendant Drafting Clerk in the Outer Department Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was transferred to Attendant Drafting Clerk in the Outer Department Office.

sentences.zh: 後坐事伏法。

translations.literal: Later he was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：仁人之言，必有博利。

translations.literal: The historian says: The words of a benevolent man must carry broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: A humane man's words ought to bring wide good.

sentences.zh: 參合之役，威罰實行，蓋王建之罪歟？

translations.literal: At the battle of Canhe Slope the awe of punishment was truly carried out—was this not Wang Jian's crime?
translations.idiomatic: At Canhe Slope terror was made real in blood—was that not Wang Jian's doing?

sentences.zh: 安同異類之人，智識入用，任等時俊，當有由哉。

translations.literal: An Tong was a man of another kind; his wisdom and knowledge were put to use, his appointments equaled the finest of the age—there must have been reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: An Tong stood apart from his kind; his wit was given room to work and he was ranked with the age's best men—surely not without cause.

sentences.zh: 頡擒赫連昌，摧義隆眾，遂為名將，未易輕也。

translations.literal: He captured Helian Chang and shattered Yilong's host, and so became a famed general—not to be lightly regarded.
translations.idiomatic: He took Helian Chang and broke Yilong's armies, earning a general's fame that none should dismiss lightly.

sentences.zh: 樓伏連、丘堆、娥清，俱以壯勇，征伐四克。

translations.literal: Lou Fulian, Qiu Dui, and E Qing—all by strength and courage conquered wherever they campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Fulian, Qiu Dui, and E Qing won their battles by sheer force of arms.

sentences.zh: 劉尼忠國翼主，豈徒驍猛之用乎？

translations.literal: Liu Ni loyally served the state and steadied his lord—is his worth only in fierce valor?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni served the throne faithfully and steadied his sovereign—was he valued only as a fighting man?

sentences.zh: 奚眷將略致位，不能以功名自終。

translations.literal: Xi Juan rose to rank by military stratagem yet could not finish his career in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Juan climbed by strategy but could not end his career in honor.

sentences.zh: 車伊洛自遠宅心，異凡戎矣。

translations.literal: Che Yiluo from afar fixed his heart on the dynasty—he was unlike ordinary barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yiluo set his heart on the dynasty from afar—no common frontier man.

sentences.zh: 宿石等並忠勤勇略，有將帥之才，自致青雲，豈徒然也。

translations.literal: Su Shi and the rest were all loyal, diligent, brave, and resourceful, with the talent of commanders; they reached the blue clouds by their own efforts—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi and his fellows were loyal, tireless, brave, and shrewd—true commanders who climbed to eminence by their own merit, not by accident.

translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

translations.idiomatic: Returned to Left Grand Master: all editions carry a spurious "right" under "left"; corrected per Beishi juan 20 (Wang Jian) and Cefu juan 352

translations.literal: Granted five thousand households of bond servants and retainers. Cefu juan 381
translations.idiomatic: Granted five thousand households of bond servants and retainers. Cefu juan 381

translations.literal: (page 4526)
reads "ten" for "thousand."
translations.idiomatic: has "ten" where the text reads "thousand."

sentences.zh: 按魏初賜奴婢、隸戶一般是數十戶，從未有這樣大的數字，如同卷安同「賜隸戶三十」，劉尼「賜別戶三十」，宿石「賜奴婢十七戶」。

translations.literal: Note: In early Wei grants of slaves and dependent households were generally on the order of several tens of households, never a figure so large—as in this same juan An Tong "granted thirty dependent households," Liu Ni "granted thirty separate households," and Su Shi "granted seventeen households of male and female slaves."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Early Wei grants of slaves and dependent households ran to a few dozen at most—never thousands—as in this same scroll: An Tong received thirty dependent households, Liu Ni thirty separate households, Su Shi seventeen slave households.

sentences.zh: 「千」字當是「十」之訛。

translations.literal: The character "thousand" must be a corruption of "ten."
translations.idiomatic: "Thousand" is almost certainly a corruption of "ten."

sentences.zh: 烏丸庫傉官鳴聚黨為寇 諸本「庫傉官鳴」作「庫侲宮鳴」。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan Kuru Guan Ming gathered a faction and became bandits. In all editions "Kuru Guan Ming" is written "Ku Zhen Gong Ming."
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan Kuru Guan Ming raised a band: all editions miswrite the name as Ku Zhen Gong Ming.

sentences.zh: 按卷二太祖紀天興元年三月記「漁陽羣盜庫傉官韜聚眾反」，七月又記「漁陽羣盜庫傉官韜復聚黨為寇，詔冠軍將軍王建討平之」。

translations.literal: According to juan 2, Annals of Emperor Taizu, third month of the first year of Tianxing: "The bandits of Yuyang, Kuru Guan Tao, gathered a multitude in revolt"; seventh month: "The bandits of Yuyang, Kuru Guan Tao, again gathered a faction and became bandits; an edict ordered General of Champion Cavalry Wang Jian to campaign and pacify them."
translations.idiomatic: Annals of Emperor Taizu, Tianxing 1, month 3: "Yuyang bandits Kuru Guan Tao gather in revolt"; month 7: "Kuru Guan Tao again raids; edict orders General of Champion Cavalry Wang Jian to suppress them."

sentences.zh: 卷一一三官氏志：「庫褥官氏，後改為庫氏。

translations.literal: Juan 113, Treatise on Clans and Surnames: "The Kuruguan clan later changed to the Ku clan.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Clans (juan 113): "The Kuruguan clan later shortened to Ku."

sentences.zh: 」「庫傉官」是烏丸姓，「傉」或作「褥」，作「辱」。

translations.literal: " "Kuru Guan" is a Wuhuan surname; the middle syllable is variously transcribed in the sources.
translations.idiomatic: "Kuruguan" is a Wuhuan surname with several alternate spellings in the manuscript tradition.

sentences.zh: 這裏「侲宮」二字顯為「傉官」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Here the two characters "Zhen Gong" are clearly a corruption of "Guan"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The characters Zhen Gong here are plainly a corruption of Guan; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其名，紀作「韜」，可能一人二名，也可能是二人，今不改。

translations.literal: The personal name in the Annals is written "Tao"; this may be one man with two names, or two men; not changed here.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals give the name as Tao—perhaps one man with two names, or two men; left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 遣斤鎮慮虒以撫慰之 諸本「慮虒」倒作「虒慮」。

translations.literal: Sent Jin to garrison Lüsi to soothe them. In all editions "Lüsi" is reversed as "Si Lü."
translations.idiomatic: Sent Jin to garrison Lüsi and pacify them: all editions reverse the place-name to Si Lü.

sentences.zh: 按「慮虒」漢縣。

translations.literal: According to "Lüsi"—a Han dynasty county.
translations.idiomatic: Lüsi was a Han county.

sentences.zh: 卷一０六上地形志上肆州永安郡驢夷條云：「二漢屬太原，曰『慮虒』，晉罷，太和十年復，改。

translations.literal: Juan 106a, Treatise on Geography, Upper, Sizhou, Yong'an Commandery, Lüyi entry says: "In the Two Han it belonged to Taiyuan and was called 'Lüsi'; abolished under Jin, restored in the tenth year of Taihe, then renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Geography (juan 106a), Sizhou, Yong'an, Lüyi: "Under the Two Han it was in Taiyuan, called Lüsi; abolished under Jin, restored Taihe 10, then renamed."

sentences.zh: 」此時縣尚未復改，承用廢縣舊名。

translations.literal: " At this time the county had not yet been restored and renamed; the old abolished name was still used.
translations.idiomatic: At this date the county had not yet been re-established under its new name; the old abolished name is used.

sentences.zh: 今乙正。

translations.literal: Now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 同長子屈 百衲本卷末有宋人校語云：「同父名屈，同長子又名屈，同雖胡人，祖孫不應同名。

translations.literal: Tong's eldest son was also named Qu. The Baipu edition at the end of the juan has a Song-dynasty collation note saying: "Tong's father was named Qu, Tong's eldest son was also named Qu; though Tong was a barbarian, grandfather and grandson ought not to share a name."
translations.idiomatic: Tong's eldest son was also named Qu. A Song note in the Baipu edition reads: "Tong's father was Qu, Tong's eldest son also Qu—even barbarians should not repeat names across generations."

sentences.zh: 」諸本無此校語，殿本入考證，却不說明是宋人語。

translations.literal: The various editions lack this note; the Dian edition includes it in textual verification but does not identify it as a Song note.
translations.idiomatic: Other editions omit the note; the Dian Kaozheng includes it without marking it as Song commentary.

sentences.zh: 按「屈」是音譯，祖孫同名是常事。

translations.literal: According to "Qu" being a phonetic transcription, grandfather and grandson sharing a name is a common occurrence.
translations.idiomatic: Qu is a transliteration; repeated names across generations were common.

sentences.zh: 至于衡關 通鑑卷一二一

translations.literal: As for Heng Pass. Zizhi tongjian juan 121
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Heng Pass. Zizhi tongjian juan 121

reads "Tong" for "Heng."
translations.idiomatic: reads Tong for Heng.

sentences.zh: 卷二五崔浩傳、卷三七司馬楚之傳敍此事都作「潼關」，冊府卷三五三

translations.literal: Juan 25, Biography of Cui Hao, and juan 37, Biography of Sima Chuzhi, both narrate this affair as "Tong Pass"; Cefu juan 353
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Cui Hao (juan 25) and Sima Chuzhi (juan 37) both say Tong Pass; Cefu juan 353

sentences.zh: 〈四一八六頁〉

translations.literal: (page 4186)

sentences.zh: 又作「衞關」。

translations.literal: again reads "Wei Pass."
translations.idiomatic: gives Wei Pass instead.

sentences.zh: 按寰宇記卷二九華陰縣潼關條引三輔記：「潼關本名衝關，河水自龍門衝激至華山東，故以名之。

translations.literal: According to Huanyu ji juan 29, Tong Pass entry in Huayin County, citing Sanfu ji: "Tong Pass was originally called Chong Pass; the river from Longmen rushes east to the foot of Mount Hua, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Huanyu ji (juan 29), Huayin, Tong Pass, citing Sanfu ji: "Originally Chong Pass—the river rushes from Longmen to Mount Hua, hence the name."

sentences.zh: 」元和志卷二潼關條亦云：「河在關內，南流衝激關山，因謂之『衝關』。

translations.literal: " Yuanhe zhi juan 2, Tong Pass entry also says: "The river within the pass flows south and rushes against the pass mountains, hence it is called 'Chong Pass.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe zhi (juan 2), Tong Pass: "The river inside the pass flows south and batters the mountains—hence Chong Pass."

sentences.zh: 」潼，廣韻亦讀尺容切，與「衝」音義俱同。

translations.literal: Tong, in Guangyun, is also read with the same initial and rhyme as "chong," and the meaning is the same as "chong."
translations.idiomatic: Tong in Guangyun shares the reading of chong in both sound and sense.

sentences.zh: 知「潼關」亦名「衝關」。

translations.literal: Thus "Tong Pass" is also called "Chong Pass."
translations.idiomatic: So Tong Pass is also Chong Pass.

sentences.zh: 這裏「衡」與冊府「衛」字都是「衝」字之訛。

translations.literal: Here "Heng" and Cefu's "Wei" are both corruptions of "Chong."
translations.idiomatic: Heng here and Wei in Cefu are both corruptions of Chong.

sentences.zh: 為北中道都大將 北史卷二五宿石傳「北」下有「征」字，按此字不應省，當是此傳脫去。

translations.literal: Made Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Middle Route. Beishi juan 25, Biography of Su Shi, has the character "Expedition" below "Northern"; this character should not be omitted and is probably lost in this biography.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Middle Route: Beishi juan 25 (Su Shi) reads Northern Expedition Route; that character was probably dropped here.

sentences.zh: 來大千 北史卷二五本傳「千」作「干」。

translations.literal: Lai Daqian. Beishi juan 25, this biography, reads "gan" for "qian."
translations.idiomatic: Lai Daqian: Beishi juan 25 writes the final character as gan instead of qian.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位 諸本「太宗」作「太祖」，北史卷二五周幾傳作「明元」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne. In all editions "Taizong" is written "Taizu"; Beishi juan 25, Biography of Zhou Ji, reads "Mingyuan."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne: all editions read Taizu; Beishi juan 25 (Zhou Ji) reads Mingyuan.

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「上已云『父千，有功太祖之世』，則此不應復云『太祖即位』，『祖』當是『宗』之誤。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai says: "Above it already says 'His father Qian had merit in Emperor Taizu's time,' so here it should not again say 'When Emperor Taizu took the throne'; 'zu' must be an error for 'zong.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai: "The text already says his father served Taizu; this line cannot again say Taizu took the throne—zu is a mistake for zong."

sentences.zh: 」按張說是，今據北史改。

translations.literal: According to Zhang's view this is correct; now changed according to Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang is right; emended per Beishi.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為子 諸本脫「爵」字，今據北史卷二五尉撥傳、冊府卷三五三

translations.literal: For merit his title was advanced to viscount. In all editions the character "title" is missing; now supplemented according to Beishi juan 25, Biography of Wei Bo, and Cefu juan 353
translations.idiomatic: For merit his title was advanced to viscount: all editions omit "title"; restored per Beishi juan 25 (Wei Bo) and Cefu juan 353

translations.literal: Supplemented.
